title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَقْتُولَةِ فِي الصُّنْدُوقِ وَالتُّفَّاحَاتِ الثَّلَاثِ
titleEn: The Girl in the Chest and the Three Apples
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 139–147 (Night 19, continuing directly from nights-18), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 19 ends the tale of the three ladies — the jinniyya disenchants the two sisters and names the caliph's own son as the husband who beat the second lady — and begins a new tale. Hārūn al-Rashīd, walking Baghdad by night with Jaʿfar and Masrūr, buys a fisherman's catch: a locked chest holding a murdered girl, cut in pieces. He gives Jaʿfar three days to find the killer or hang; a youth and an old man each confess. The youth tells how his wife, sick and longing for an apple, was killed on the word of a black slave who boasted of having her apple, and how his son's account proved her innocent too late. Verse is copied as printed. The night ends as the caliph vows to hang the slave, and dawn cuts Shahrazad off. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularized the language here and there, so some of the original Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ التَّاسِعَةَ عَشْرَ قَالَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-tāsiʿata ʿashara qālat
sentences.l: And when was the night the nineteenth, she said:
sentences.i: And when it was the nineteenth night, she said:
sentences.n: This is the regular night-opening formula. عشر is printed without the feminine ة that an ordinal compound with a feminine noun would take (عَشْرَةَ); it is vocalised as printed. The compound التَّاسِعَةَ عَشْرَ is fixed in -a whatever its case.

sentences.t: بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ أَمَرَأَنْ تُكْتَبَ هَذِةِ الْقِصَّةُ فِي الدَّوَاوِينِ وَيَجْعَلُوهَا فِي خِزَانَةِ الْمَلِكِ
sentences.tr: balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-khalīfata amara an tuktaba hādhihi al-qiṣṣatu fī al-dawāwīni wa-yajʿalūhā fī khizānati al-maliki
sentences.l: It reached me, O king, the fortunate, that the caliph commanded that be-written this story in the registers, and they-place-it in the treasury of-the-king.
sentences.i: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the caliph commanded that this story be written down in the record-books and that it be placed in the king's library.
sentences.n: أَمَرَأَنْ is printed as one word (أمر + أن run together). تُكْتَبَ is passive, with the story as its subject; the next verb وَيَجْعَلُوهَا has an unnamed "they" (the scribes and officials), still governed by أَنْ, with the nūn dropped. The edition prints هذة with final ة for ه throughout, so the ة carries the vowel here (هَذِةِ) and is read hādhihi.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ قَالَ لِلصَّبِيَّةِ الْأُولَى هَلْ عِنْدَكِ خَبَرٌ مِنَ الْعِفْرِيتَةِ الَّتِي سَحَرَتْ إِخْوَانَكِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu qāla li-al-ṣabiyyati al-ūlā hal ʿindaki khabarun mina al-ʿifrītati allatī saḥarat ikhwānaki
sentences.l: Then indeed-he said to-the-girl the first: "Is-there with-you news from the she-ifrit who enchanted your brothers?"
sentences.i: Then he said to the first girl, "Have you any news of the she-ifrit who enchanted your sisters?"
sentences.n: إِخْوَانَكِ is the masculine plural "brothers" but here means siblings: the two enchanted are her sisters (a later line calls them أَخَوَاتُهَا).

sentences.t: قَالَتْ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِنَّهَا أَعْطَتْنِي شَيْأً مِنْ شَعْرِهَا وَقَٰلَتْ
sentences.tr: qālat yā amīra al-muʾminīna innahā aʿṭatnī shayʾan min shaʿrihā wa-qālat
sentences.l: She said: "O Commander of the Faithful, indeed-she gave-me something of her hair, and she-said:
sentences.i: She said, "Commander of the Faithful, she gave me a little of her hair, and said:
sentences.n: The edition prints وقلت, which could be read وَقُلْتُ "and I said" (the jinniyya's own voice slipping into the report, as حضوري "my presence" follows). Since the girl is reporting what the jinniyya told her, it is read here with a dagger alif as وَقَالَتْ "and she said".

sentences.t: مَتَى أَرَدْتِي حُضُورِي فَأَحْرِقِي مِنْ هَذَا الشَّعْرِ شَعْرَةً فَأَحْضُرَ إِلَيْكِ عَاجِلًا وَلَوْ كُنْتُ خَلْفَ جَبَلِ قَافٍ
sentences.tr: matā aradtī ḥuḍūrī fa-aḥriqī min hādhā al-shaʿri shaʿratan fa-aḥḍura ilayki ʿājilan wa-law kuntu khalfa jabali Qāfin
sentences.l: Whenever you-wished my-presence, then burn from this hair a-hair, and I-be-present to-you swiftly, even-if I-were behind the mountain of-Qāf."
sentences.i: Whenever you wish my presence, burn one hair of this hair, and I shall come to you at once, even if I were beyond Mount Qāf."
sentences.n: أَرَدْتِي is printed with an extra final ي on the feminine "you" (-ti); a Middle Arabic spelling, read -ti. Mount Qāf is the legendary mountain ringing the whole earth. فَأَحْضُرَ is subjunctive because it follows a command with فَـ of consequence.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ أَحْضِرِي لِي الشَّعْرَ فَأَحْضَرَتْهُ الصَّبِيَّةُ فَأَخَذَةُ الْخَلِيفَةُ وَحَرَقَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu aḥḍirī lī al-shaʿra fa-aḥḍarat-hu al-ṣabiyyatu fa-akhadhahu al-khalīfatu wa-ḥaraqahu
sentences.l: So said the caliph: "Bring to-me the hair." So brought-it the girl, so took-it the caliph and burned-it.
sentences.i: The caliph said, "Bring me the hair," and the girl brought it; the caliph took it and burned it.
sentences.n: فَأَخَذَةُ has a final ة printed for the pronoun ـهُ ("it"), as with هذة; the ة is given the vowel the pronoun would have and the word is read akhadhahu.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا ظَهَرَتْ رَائِحَتُهُ اهْتَزَّ الْقَصْرُ وَسَمِعُوا دَوِيًّا وَقَرْقَعَةً وَإِذَا بِالْجِنِّيَّةِ حَضَرَتْ وَكَانَتْ مُسْلِمَةً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ẓaharat rāʾiḥatuhu ihtazza al-qaṣru wa-samiʿū dawiyyan wa-qarqaʿatan wa-idhā bi-al-jinniyyati ḥaḍarat wa-kānat muslimatan
sentences.l: So when appeared its-smell, shook the palace, and they-heard a-rumbling and a-clattering, and-behold — with-the-jinn-woman — she-had-arrived, and she-was a-Muslim.
sentences.i: When its smell rose, the palace shook, and they heard a rumbling and a clatter; and behold, the she-jinni had arrived, and she was a Muslim.
sentences.n: The بِـ in وَإِذَا بِالْجِنِّيَّةِ only marks what suddenly appears, as it always does after إِذَا of surprise. قرقعة is imitative: a rattling, crashing noise.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا خَلِيفَةَ اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-salāmu ʿalayka yā khalīfata Allāhi
sentences.l: So she said: "The peace upon you, O deputy of-God!"
sentences.i: She said, "Peace be upon you, O caliph of God."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ وَ رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَانُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-ʿalaykumu al-salāmu wa-raḥmatu Allāhi wa-barakānuhu
sentences.l: So he said: "And upon-you-all the peace, and the mercy of-God and his blessings."
sentences.i: He said, "And upon you be peace, and God's mercy and blessings."
sentences.n: The plural عَلَيْكُمُ is the normal courtesy form of the reply even to one person. The edition prints وبركانه with ن where the formula has ت (وَبَرَكَاتُهُ); it is vocalised as printed and would be read barakātuhu.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ اعْلَمْ أَنَّ هَذِةِ الصَّبِيَّةَ زَرَعَتْ مَعِيَ جَمِيلًا وَلَا أَقْدِرُ أُكَافِيهَا عَلَيْهِ وَهِيَ أَنْقَذَتْنِي مِنَ الْمَوْتِ وَقَتَلَتْ عَدُوِّي
sentences.tr: fa-qālati iʿlam anna hādhihi al-ṣabiyyata zaraʿat maʿiya jamīlan wa-lā aqdiru ukāfiyahā ʿalayhi wa-hiya anqadhatnī mina al-mawti wa-qatalat ʿaduwwī
sentences.l: So she said: "Know that this girl sowed with-me a-fair-deed, and I-am-not able I-repay-her for-it; and she rescued-me from the death and killed my-enemy.
sentences.i: She said, "Know that this girl sowed a kindness with me which I cannot repay: she saved me from death and killed my enemy.
sentences.n: "To sow a fair deed" is to do a good turn. أُكَافِيهَا is from كَافَأَ "to requite", with the hamza written as ي; the verb follows أَقْدِرُ directly with no أَنْ, a common colloquial-leaning construction.

sentences.t: وَرَأَيْتُ مَا فَعَلَتْ مَعَهَا أَخَوَاتُهَا فَمَا رَأَيْتُ إِلَّا أَنِّي أَنْتَقِمُ مِنْهُمْ وَأَسْحَرُهُمْ كِلَابًا بَعْدَ أَنْ أَرَدْتُ قَتْلَهُمْ فَخَشِيتُ أَنْ يَصْعُبَ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-raʾaytu mā faʿalat maʿahā akhawātuhā fa-mā raʾaytu illā annī antaqimu minhum wa-asḥaruhum kilāban baʿda an aradtu qatlahum fa-khashītu an yaṣʿuba ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And I-saw what did with-her her-sisters, and I-saw-not except that-I take-revenge on-them and enchant-them dogs, after that I-wanted their-killing; then I-feared that it-be-hard on-her.
sentences.i: I saw what her sisters had done to her, and I saw no course but to take vengeance on them and enchant them into dogs, after I had meant to kill them; but I feared it would grieve her.

sentences.t: وَالْآنَ إِنْ أَرَدْتَ خَلَاصَهُمْ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أُخَلِّصْهُمْ كَرَامَةً لَكَ وَلَهَا فَإِنِّي مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-al-āna in aradta khalāṣahum yā amīra al-muʾminīna ukhalliṣhum karāmatan laka wa-lahā fa-innī mina al-muslimīna
sentences.l: And now, if you-wanted their-deliverance, O Commander of-the-Faithful, I-free-them, as-an-honour to-you and to-her, for indeed-I am among the Muslims.
sentences.i: And now, Commander of the Faithful, if you wish them delivered, I shall free them, out of respect for you and for her; for I am one of the Muslims.
sentences.n: أُخَلِّصْهُمْ is the answer to إِنْ, put in the jussive without فَـ. كَرَامَةً is an accusative of reason: "out of honour to".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا خَلِّصِيهِمْ وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ نَشْرَعُ فِي أَمْرِ الصَّبِيَّةِ الْمَضْرُوبَةِ وَنَفْحَصُ عَنْ حَالِهَا فَإِذَا ظَهَرَلِي صِدْقُهَا أَخَذْتُ ثَرْهَا مِمَّنْ ظَلَمَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā khalliṣīhim wa-baʿda dhālika nashraʿu fī amri al-ṣabiyyati al-maḍrūbati wa-nafḥaṣu ʿan ḥālihā fa-idhā ẓahara lī ṣidquhā akhadhtu thaʾrahā mimman ẓalamahā
sentences.l: So he said to-her: "Free-them; and after that we-begin in the matter of-the-girl the beaten-one, and we-examine about her state; and when appears to-me her truthfulness, I-take her vengeance from-him-who wronged-her."
sentences.i: He said to her, "Free them; after that we shall take up the case of the beaten girl and inquire into her circumstances, and if her truthfulness is made plain to me, I shall exact her vengeance from whoever wronged her."
sentences.n: ظَهَرَلِي is printed as one word (ظهر + لي). ثرها is printed without the alif; the word meant is ثَأْرُهَا / ثَأْرَهَا, "her blood-vengeance", so it is vocalised over the letters printed and translated as thaʾrahā.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْعِفْرِينَةُ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ هَا أَنَا أُخَلِّصُهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-ʿifrīnatu yā amīra al-muʾminīna hā anā ukhalliṣuhum
sentences.l: So said the she-ifrit: "O Commander of-the-Faithful, behold I — I-free-them,
sentences.i: The she-ifrit said, "Commander of the Faithful, here I am; I shall free them,
sentences.n: العفرينة is printed with ن for the ت of العفريتة (which the text spells correctly a few words on); it is vocalised as printed and read al-ʿifrīta.

sentences.t: وَأَدُلُّكَ عَلَى مَنْ فَعَلَ بِهَذِةِ الصَّبِيَّةِ وَظَلَمَهَا وَأَخَذَ مَالَهَا وَهُوَ أَقْرَبُ النَّاسِ إِلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: wa-adullaka ʿalā man faʿala bi-hādhihi al-ṣabiyyati wa-ẓalamahā wa-akhadha mālahā wa-huwa aqrabu al-nāsi ilayka
sentences.l: and I-guide-you to him-who did to this girl and wronged-her and took her wealth, and he (is) the nearest of-the-people to-you."
sentences.i: and I shall show you who did this to the girl, wronged her and took her property; he is the nearest of all men to you."

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْعِفْرِيتَةَ أَخَذَتْ طَاسَةً مِنَ الْمَاءِ وَعَزَمَتْ عَلَيْهَا وَتَكَلَّمَتْ بِكَلَامٍ لَا أَفْهَمُ وَرَشَّتْ وَجْهَ الْكَلْبَتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ʿifrītata akhadhat ṭāsatan mina al-māʾi wa-ʿazamat ʿalayhā wa-takallamat bi-kalāmin lā afhamu wa-rashshat wajha al-kalbatayni
sentences.l: Then indeed the she-ifrit took a-bowl of the water, and conjured over-it, and spoke with-speech I-do-not-understand, and sprinkled the face of-the-two-bitches.
sentences.i: Then the she-ifrit took a bowl of water, pronounced an incantation over it, spoke words I cannot understand, and sprinkled the faces of the two bitches.
sentences.n: عَزَمَ عَلَى is "to conjure over". The verb لَا أَفْهَمُ is in the first person: the storyteller (Shahrazad) steps in to say the spell was not understood. وَجْهَ is a singular for the two faces.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُمْ عُودُوا إِلَى صُورَتِكُمُ الْأُولَى الْبَشَرِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahum ʿūdū ilā ṣūratikumu al-ūlā al-bashariyyati
sentences.l: And she said to-them: "Return to your-form the first, the human."
sentences.i: and said to them, "Return to your first shape, the human one."
sentences.n: لَهُمْ and عُودُوا are masculine plural although the two are female: the plural of address ignores gender, and the verbs below agree.

sentences.t: فَعَادُوا إِلَى صُورَتِهِمُ الَّتِي كَانُوا عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿādū ilā ṣūratihimu allatī kānū ʿalayhā
sentences.l: So they-returned to their-form which they-were upon-it.
sentences.i: and they returned to the shape they had had before.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَٰلَتِ الْعِفْرِيتَةُ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِنَّ الَّذِي ضَرَبَ الصَّبِيَّةَ وَلَدُكَ الْأَمِينُ أَخُ الْمَأْمُونِ
sentences.tr: thumma qālati al-ʿifrītatu yā amīra al-muʾminīna inna alladhī ḍaraba al-ṣabiyyata waladuka al-amīnu akhu al-maʾmūni
sentences.l: Then said the she-ifrit: "O Commander of-the-Faithful, indeed the-one-who struck the girl (is) your-son al-Amīn, brother of-al-Maʾmūn.
sentences.i: Then the she-ifrit said, "Commander of the Faithful, the man who beat the girl is your son al-Amīn, the brother of al-Maʾmūn.
sentences.n: The edition prints قلت for قالت; it takes the dagger alif here. Al-Amīn and al-Maʾmūn are Hārūn al-Rashīd's two sons, historically rivals for the caliphate. أَخُ is printed short, without the و of the construct form أَخُو.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهُ كَانَ يَسْمَعُ بِحُسْنِهَا وَجَمَالِهَا وَنَصَبَ عَلَيْهَا حِيلَةً وَتَزَوَّجَهَا بِالْحَلَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-innahu kāna yasmaʿu bi-ḥusnihā wa-jamālihā wa-naṣaba ʿalayhā ḥīlatan wa-tazawwajahā bi-al-ḥalāli
sentences.l: For indeed-he was hearing of her-beauty and her-loveliness, and set-up against-her a-ruse, and married-her by-the-lawful.
sentences.i: He had heard of her beauty and loveliness, and laid a stratagem for her, and married her lawfully.
sentences.n: سَمِعَ بِـ is "to hear of". نَصَبَ عَلَيْهَا حِيلَةً is to set a trap for her. بِالْحَلَالِ: by lawful means, in proper wedlock.

sentences.t: وَهُوَ مَالَهُ ذَنْبٌ فِي ضَرْبِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-huwa mā lahu dhanbun fī ḍarbihā
sentences.l: And he — not-to-him a-fault in her-beating;
sentences.i: and he is not at fault in beating her,
sentences.n: مَالَهُ is printed as one word and is read مَا لَهُ "there is not to him": ما negating a nominal clause, as in colloquial Arabic. It could also be read mālahu "his property", but that gives no sense here.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهُ اشْتَرَطَ عَلَيْهَا وَحَلَّفَهَا أَيْمَانًا عَظِيمَةً أَنْ لَا تَفْعَلَ شَيْئًا وَقَدْ خَانَتِ الْيَمِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-innahu ishtaraṭa ʿalayhā wa-ḥallafahā aymānan ʿaẓīmatan an lā tafʿala shayʾan wa-qad khānati al-yamīna
sentences.l: for indeed-he stipulated upon-her and made-her-swear great oaths that not she-do anything; and indeed she-betrayed the oath.
sentences.i: for he laid a condition on her and made her swear mighty oaths that she would do nothing, and she has broken the oath.
sentences.n: The edition leaves شَيْئًا unspecified: she swore to do nothing (forbidden, the story supplies elsewhere). حَلَّفَ takes two accusatives, the person and the oaths.

sentences.t: فَأَرَادَ قَتْلَهَا فَخَافَ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى فَضَرَبَهَا هَذَا الضَّرْبَ وَأَعَادَهَا إِلَى مَكَانِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-arāda qatlahā fa-khāfa Allāha taʿālā fa-ḍarabahā hādhā al-ḍarba wa-aʿādahā ilā makānihā
sentences.l: So he-wanted her-killing, but feared God (exalted-is-He), so beat-her this beating, and returned-her to her-place.
sentences.i: He wanted to kill her, but feared God Most High; so he beat her with the beating you have seen, and sent her back to her place.
sentences.n: هَذَا الضَّرْبَ is a cognate accusative, "this beating", pointing to the one just described earlier in the tale.

sentences.t: وَهَذِهِ قِصَّةُ الْبِنْتِ الثَّانِيَةِ وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhihi qiṣṣatu al-bint al-thāniyati wa-Allāhu aʿlamu
sentences.l: And this (is) the story of-the-girl the second, and God (is) most-knowing.
sentences.i: And this is the story of the second girl; and God knows best.
sentences.n: وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ ("and God knows best") is the standard formula for closing an account.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْخَلِيفَةُ ذَلِكَ مِنْ كَلَامِ الْعِفْرِيتَةِ وَعَلِمَ ضَرْبَ الصَّبِيَّةِ تَعَجَّبَ كُلَّ الْعَجَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-khalīfatu dhālika min kalāmi al-ʿifrītati wa-ʿalima ḍarba al-ṣabiyyati taʿajjaba kulla al-ʿajabi
sentences.l: And when the caliph heard that from the speech of the she-ifrit and knew the striking of the girl, he marvelled the whole of the marvelling.
sentences.i: When the caliph heard all this from the words of the she-ifrit and learned of the girl's beating, he marvelled with the utmost wonder.
sentences.n: كُلَّ الْعَجَبِ is an adverbial accusative: literally "the whole of wonder", i.e. as much wonder as could be. الْعِفْرِيتَةِ is the she-ifrit (a powerful female jinn) who has just told the tale.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ الَّذِي مَنَّ عَلَيَّ بِهَذَا وَتَخَلَّصَ الْبِنْتَيْنِ مِنَ السِّحْرِ وَالْعَذَابِ وَمَنَّ عَلَيَّ بِخَبَرِ هَذِهِ الصَّبِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla subḥāna Allāhi al-ʿaliyyi al-ʿaẓīmi alladhī manna ʿalayya bi-hādhā wa-takhallaṣa al-bintayni mina al-siḥri wa-al-ʿadhābi wa-manna ʿalayya bi-khabari hādhihi al-ṣabiyyati
sentences.l: And he said: Glory (be) to God, the exalted, the mighty, who bestowed-favour upon me with this, and freed the two girls from the sorcery and the torment, and bestowed-favour upon me with the news of this girl.
sentences.i: And he said: Glory to God, the Most High, the Almighty, who has favoured me with this, delivered the two girls from enchantment and torment, and favoured me also with the tidings of this girl.
sentences.n: وَتَخَلَّصَ is the printed تخلص, which I read as the fifth-form verb تَخَلَّصَ; that form normally means "got free", so with an object (الْبِنْتَيْنِ) it is a Middle Arabic use for the second-form خَلَّصَ "freed". The other reading, a verbal noun after بِهَذَا, does not fit the spelling. مَنَّ عَلَى "do a favour to" takes بِـ for the favour itself.

sentences.t: وَاللَّهِ لَأَعْمَلَنَّ عَمَلًا يُكْتَبُ بَعْدِي
sentences.tr: wa-Allāhi la-aʿmalanna ʿamalan yuktabu baʿdī
sentences.l: And by God, I will surely do a deed (that) is written after me.
sentences.i: By God, I shall do a deed that will be recorded after I am gone.
sentences.n: The وَ of oath (وَاللَّهِ) is answered by لَـ with the emphatic nūn: لَأَعْمَلَنَّ "I will surely do".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَحْضَرَ وَلَدَهُ الْأَمِينَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَسَأَلَهُ عَنْ قِصَّةِ الصَّبِيَّةِ الْأُولَى فَأَخْبَرَهُ عَلَى وَجْهِ الْحَقِّ
sentences.tr: thumma aḥḍara waladahu al-amīna bayna yadayhi wa-saʾalahu ʿan qiṣṣati al-ṣabiyyati al-ūlā fa-akhbarahu ʿalā wajhi al-ḥaqqi
sentences.l: Then he had-brought his son al-Amīn between his two hands, and asked him about the story of the first girl, and he told him upon the face of the truth.
sentences.i: Then he summoned his son al-Amīn into his presence and questioned him about the story of the first girl, and he told him the whole matter truthfully.
sentences.n: بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ, "between his two hands", is the standard idiom for "in his presence". The son al-Amīn is the beaten girl's husband, as the unit after next shows.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَحْضَرَ الْقُضَاةَ وَالشُّهُودَ وَأَحْضَرَ الْقَرَنْدَلِيَّةَ الثَّلَٰثَةَ وَأَحْضَرَ الصَّبِيَّةَ الْأُولَى وَأَخَوَاتِهَا اللَّتَيْنِ كَانَتَا مَسْحُورَتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: thumma aḥḍara al-quḍāta wa-al-shuhūda wa-aḥḍara al-qarandaliyyata al-thalāthata wa-aḥḍara al-ṣabiyyata al-ūlā wa-akhawātihā allatayni kānatā masḥūratayni
sentences.l: Then he had-brought the judges and the witnesses, and had-brought the three qarandalī-ones (Qalandars), and had-brought the first girl and her sisters, the two who had been two-bewitched-ones.
sentences.i: Then he summoned the judges and the witnesses, and the three Qalandars, and the first girl with her two sisters who had been bewitched.
sentences.n: الثَّلَٰثَةَ is the edition's defective spelling الثلثة for الثلاثة; the small dagger alif shows the long vowel. الْقَرَنْدَلِيَّةَ (printed with rāʾ) are Qalandars, wandering dervishes, here the three men who had been kings. Three verbs of summoning in a row open with the same أَحْضَرَ.

sentences.t: وَزَوَّجَ الثَّلَٰتَ لِلثَّلَٰثَةِ الْقَرَنْدَلِيَّةِ الَّذِينَ أَخْبَرُوا أَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا مُلُوكًا وَعَمِلَهُمْ حُجَّابًا عِنْدَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-zawwaja al-thalāta li-al-thalāthati al-qarandaliyyati alladhīna akhbarū annahum kānū mulūkan wa-ʿamilahum ḥujjāban ʿindahu
sentences.l: And he gave-in-marriage the three (women) to the three Qalandars, who had told (that) they had been kings, and made them chamberlains with him.
sentences.i: And he married the three women to the three Qalandars, who had declared that they had once been kings, and he made them chamberlains at his court.
sentences.n: الثَّلَٰتَ is printed with tāʾ (الثلت) where thāʾ is meant; I keep the printed letters and vocalise the word as the feminine "three" (thalāth). عَمِلَهُمْ حُجَّابًا uses ʿamila "do, make" for Classical جَعَلَهُمْ, a Middle Arabic habit.

sentences.t: وَ أَعْطَاهُمْ مَا يَحْتَاجُونَ إِلَيْهِ وَأَجْرَى لَهُمْ جَرَايَاتٍ وَأَنْزَلَهُمْ فِي قَصْرِ بَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: wa-aʿṭāhum mā yaḥtājūna ilayhi wa-ajrā lahum jarāyātin wa-anzalahum fī qaṣri Baghdāda
sentences.l: And he gave them what they needed to it, and caused-to-flow for them allowances, and lodged them in the palace of Baghdad.
sentences.i: He gave them all that they needed, settled allowances upon them, and lodged them in the palace at Baghdad.
sentences.n: The edition prints this وَ detached from the next word, at the line break; it is simply the ordinary "and". أَجْرَى لَهُمْ جَرَايَاتٍ: "he made allowances run for them", i.e. assigned regular rations.

sentences.t: وَرَدَّ الصَّبِيَّةَ الْمَضْرُوبَةَ لِوَلَدِهِ الْأَمِينِ وَجَدَّدَ كِتَابَهُ وَأَعْطَاهَا مَالًا كَثِيرًا
sentences.tr: wa-radda al-ṣabiyyata al-maḍrūbata li-waladihi al-amīni wa-jaddada kitābahu wa-aʿṭāhā mālan kathīran
sentences.l: And he returned the beaten girl to his son al-Amīn, and renewed his writing, and gave her much wealth.
sentences.i: He restored the beaten girl to his son al-Amīn, renewed the marriage contract, and gave her great wealth.
sentences.n: كِتَابَهُ "his writing" is most likely the marriage contract (kitāb), renewed now that the couple are reunited; the text does not say so outright.

sentences.t: وَأَمَرَ أَنْ تُبْنَى الدَّارُ أَحْسَنَ مَا كَانَتْ
sentences.tr: wa-amara an tubnā al-dāru aḥsana mā kānat
sentences.l: And he commanded that the house be built (as) the best of what it had been.
sentences.i: He ordered the house rebuilt finer than it had ever been.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا الْخَلِيفَةُ فَقَدْ تَزَوَّجَ بِالْخُشْكَاشَةِ وَرَقَدَ فِي تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةِ مَعَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-khalīfatu fa-qad tazawwaja bi-al-khushkāshati wa-raqada fī tilka al-laylati maʿahā
sentences.l: And as for the caliph, he had married the Khushkāsha, and lay down in that night with her.
sentences.i: As for the caliph, he took the Khushkāsha in marriage and lay with her that night.
sentences.n: تَزَوَّجَ بِـ "marry" with بِـ is Middle Arabic; Classical uses the bare accusative. الْخُشْكَاشَةِ is a woman's epithet or name whose meaning is uncertain; it may go back to Persian khushk "dry" (compare خُشْكَارٌ, coarse bread), but I cannot confirm that.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ أَفْرَدَ لَهَا بَيْتًا وَجَوَارِيَ لِخِدْمَتِهَا وَرَتَّبَ لَهَا رَوَاتِبَ وَجَعَلَ لَهَا بَيْتًا بِسَرَارِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa afrada lahā baytan wa-jawāriya li-khidmatihā wa-rattaba lahā rawātiba wa-jaʿala lahā baytan bi-sarārīhi
sentences.l: And when he entered-the-morning, he set-apart for her a house, and slave-girls for her service, and arranged for her stipends, and made for her a house with his concubines.
sentences.i: In the morning he set apart a house for her, with maidservants to wait on her, fixed a regular allowance for her, and gave her an apartment among his concubines.
sentences.n: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ, "and when morning came", is a stock way of moving the story forward to the next day.

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبَ النَّاسُ مِنْ كَرَمِ الْخَلِيفَةِ وَسَمَاحَةِ نَفْسِهِ وَحِكْمَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjaba al-nāsu min karami al-khalīfati wa-samāḥati nafsihi wa-ḥikmatihi
sentences.l: And the people marvelled at the generosity of the caliph and the liberality of his soul and his wisdom.
sentences.i: And the people marvelled at the caliph's generosity, his openhandedness, and his wisdom.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَ الْخَلِيفَةُ أَنْ يُؤَرِّخُوا قِصَصَ هَؤُلَاءِ جَمِيعِهِمْ
sentences.tr: thumma amara al-khalīfatu an yuʾarrikhū qiṣaṣa hāʾulāʾi jamīʿihim
sentences.l: Then the caliph commanded that they record the stories of these, all of them.
sentences.i: Then the caliph ordered that the stories of all these people be set down in the chronicles.
sentences.n: The subject of يُؤَرِّخُوا is left unnamed ("they"), the scribes of the court.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ دُنْيَازَادُ لِأُخْتِهَا شَهْرَزَادَ يَا أُخْتَاهُ وَاللَّهِ هَذِهِ قِصَّةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ لَطِيفَةٌ لَا يُسْمَعُ مِثْلُهَا قَطُّ
sentences.tr: qālat Dunyāzādu li-ukhtihā Shahrazāda yā ukhtāhu wa-Allāhi hādhihi qiṣṣatun jamīlatun laṭīfatun lā yusmaʿu mithluhā qaṭṭu
sentences.l: Dunyāzād said to her sister Shahrazād: O my sister, by God, this (is) a story beautiful, delicate, the like of which is never heard.
sentences.i: Dunyāzād said to her sister Shahrazād: Sister, by God, this is a lovely and graceful tale, the like of which has never been heard.
sentences.n: Here the frame story resumes: the tale of the Three Ladies is over, and Dunyāzād asks her sister for another. يَا أُخْتَاهُ is the vocative "O my sister" with the lengthening ending -āh.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنِ احْكِي لِي قِصَّةً أُخْرَيٰ لِنَقْضِيَ مَا بَقِيَ مِنْ سَهَرِ لَيْلَتِنَا هَذَا
sentences.tr: wa-lākini iḥkī lī qiṣṣatan ukhrā li-naqḍiya mā baqiya min sahari laylatinā hādhā
sentences.l: But tell to me another story, so that we may pass what remained of the wakefulness of our night this.
sentences.i: But tell me another tale, that we may spend what is left of the waking hours of this night of ours.
sentences.n: لَيْلَتِنَا هَذَا pairs a feminine noun with the masculine demonstrative; Classical would have هَذِهِ. The unit keeps what is printed. The lām of لِنَقْضِيَ is the "so that" lām and takes the subjunctive.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ حُبًّا وَكَرَامَةً إِنْ أَدِنَ لِي الْمَلِكُ
sentences.tr: qālat ḥubban wa-karāmatan in adina lī al-maliku
sentences.l: She said: With love and honour, if the king gave-permission to me.
sentences.i: She said: Gladly and with honour, if the king permits me.
sentences.n: أَدِنَ is printed ادن with dāl; the verb meant is أَذِنَ "gave permission", so this is a slip or a dialect confusion of dāl and dhāl. I keep the printed letter and read adhina.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ قُصِّي قِصَّتَكِ وَأَعْجِلِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku quṣṣī qiṣṣataki wa-aʿjilī
sentences.l: And the king said: Narrate your story, and hasten.
sentences.i: The king said: Tell your tale, and be quick.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ زَعَمُوا يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ وَصَاحِبَ الْعَصْرِ وَالْأَوَانِ أَنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ هَارُونَ الرَّشِيدَ أَحْضَرَ لَيْلَةً مِنَ اللَّيَالِي وَزِيرَهُ جَعْفَرًا وَقَالَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat zaʿamū yā malika al-zamāni wa-ṣāḥiba al-ʿaṣri wa-al-awāni anna al-khalīfata Hārūna al-Rashīda aḥḍara laylatan mina al-layālī wazīrahu Jaʿfaran wa-qāla lahu
sentences.l: And she said: They claimed, O king of the time and master of the age and the epoch, that the caliph Hārūn al-Rashīd summoned, one night of the nights, his vizier Jaʿfar, and said to him:
sentences.i: And she said: It is related, O king of the age, lord of the era and the hour, that one night the caliph Hārūn al-Rashīd summoned his vizier Jaʿfar and said to him:
sentences.n: زَعَمُوا "they claimed" is the storyteller's way of saying "it is told", without vouching for the tale. الزَّمَانِ ... الْأَوَانِ rhyme on -ān (sajʿ). In the vocative construct يَا مَلِكَ, مَلِكَ is accusative.

sentences.t: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَنْزِلَ الْمَدِينَةَ وَ نَسْأَلَ الْعَامَّةَ عَنْ أَحْوَالِ الْحُكَّامِ الْمُتَوَلِّينَ
sentences.tr: urīdu an anzila al-madīnata wa-nasʾala al-ʿāmmata ʿan aḥwāli al-ḥukkāmi al-mutawallīna
sentences.l: I want that I go-down (to) the city and ask the common-people about the conditions of the governors, the ones-in-charge.
sentences.i: I wish to go down into the city and ask the common people how the governors in office are faring.
sentences.n: The printed وَ stands apart from نَسْأَلَ at a line break; it is the ordinary "and". أَنْزِلَ takes a direct object (الْمَدِينَةَ) where Classical would use إِلَى. نَسْأَلَ is subjunctive, still governed by أَنْ.

sentences.t: وَكُلُّ مَنْ شَكَوْامِنْهُ عَزَلْنَاهُ وَمَنْ شَكَرُوا مِنْهُ أَوْلَیْنَاهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kullu man shakaw minhu ʿazalnāhu wa-man shakarū minhu awlaynāhu
sentences.l: And every one of-whom they complained of him, we dismissed him; and whoever they thanked of him, we conferred (office) on him.
sentences.i: Whoever they complain of, we will dismiss; and whoever they praise, we will confirm in office.
sentences.n: شَكَوْامِنْهُ is printed as a single word (شكوامنه) with no space; it is شَكَوْا مِنْهُ "they complained of him". The perfect tenses عَزَلْنَاهُ and أَوْلَیْنَاهُ have conditional, future force, the usual way of stating a rule. أَوْلَیْنَاهُ is printed with the Persian-style dotted final-ی: the printed letters are kept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ جَعْفَرٌ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Jaʿfarun samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: And Jaʿfar said: Hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: And Jaʿfar answered with hearing and obedience.
sentences.n: The stock formula of assent to a superior, an accusative of manner with the verb ("I offer") left out.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَزَلَ الْخَلِيفَةُ وَجَعْفَرٌ وَمَسْرُورٌ وَشَقُّوا فِى الْمَدِينَةِ وَمَشَوْا فِى الْأَسْوَاقِ وَ الشَّوَارِعِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā nazala al-khalīfatu wa-Jaʿfarun wa-Masrūrun wa-shaqqū fī al-madīnati wa-mashaw fī al-aswāqi wa-al-shawāriʿi
sentences.l: And when the caliph and Jaʿfar and Masrūr went-down, and cut-through the city, and walked in the markets and the streets,
sentences.i: When the caliph, Jaʿfar and Masrūr had gone down and made their way through the city, walking in the markets and the streets,
sentences.n: Masrūr is the caliph's attendant, his executioner in the Nights. The verbs turn plural (شَقُّوا, مَشَوْا) after the singular نَزَلَ. The printed وَ before الشَّوَارِعِ is detached at a line break.

sentences.t: فَاجْتَازُوا عَلَى زُقَاقٍ فَرَأَوْا شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا عَلَى رَأْسِهِ شَبَكَةٌ وَقُفَّةٌ وَ فِي يَدِهِ عَصًا وَهُوَ مَاشٍ عَلَى مَهْلِهِ يُنْشِدُ وَيَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-ijtāzū ʿalā zuqāqin fa-raʾaw shaykhan kabīran ʿalā raʾsihi shabakatun wa-quffatun wa-fī yadihi ʿaṣan wa-huwa māshin ʿalā mahlihi yunshidu wa-yaqūlu
sentences.l: they passed by an alley, and saw an old man, great (in age), on his head a net and a basket, and in his hand a staff, and he walking at his leisure, reciting and saying:
sentences.i: they came upon an alley and saw a very old man with a net and a basket on his head and a staff in his hand, walking at his ease and reciting as he went:
sentences.n: شَبَكَةٌ is a net; whether a fisherman's net, a hair-net or a carrying net is not clear from the text. قُفَّةٌ is a basket. The verses he recites follow immediately. The printed وَ before فِي is detached at a line break.

sentences.t:
يَقُولُونَ لِي أَنْتَ بَيْنَ الْوَرِي * بِعِلْمِكَ كَاللَّيْلَةِ الْمُقْمِرَةِ
فَقُلْتُ دَعُونِي مِنْ أَقْوَالِكُمْ * فَلَا عِلْمَ إِلَّا مَعَ الْمَقْدِرَةِ
sentences.tr:
yaqūlūna lī anta bayna al-warā * bi-ʿilmika ka-al-laylati al-muqmirati
fa-qultu daʿūnī min aqwālikum * fa-lā ʿilma illā maʿa al-maqdirati
sentences.l:
They-say to-me: you, among the creation, * in-your-knowledge, are like-the-night the-moonlit.
So I-said: leave-me from your-sayings, * for no knowledge except with the-ability.
sentences.i: They say to me: "Among mankind, for your learning, you are like a moonlit night." * And I answered: "Leave me be with your speeches, for there is no learning without the means to back it."
sentences.n: بِعِلْمِكَ is a bare prepositional phrase with the predicate ("you are") left to be understood; كَـ in كَاللَّيْلَةِ is the comparative "like". الْمَقْدِرَةُ (also مَقْدُرَة) is ability, and here means means or resources, i.e. money. The couplet rhymes on -ra-ti.

sentences.t:
فَلَوْ رَهَنُونِي وَعِلْمِي مَعِي * وَكُلِّ اللِّفَا تَرْوِ الْمِحْبَرَةِ
عَلَى قُوتِ يَوْمٍ فَرُدَّ الرِّهَانُ * وَارْمُوا إِلَى الْقِصَّةِ الْمَقَرَّةِ
sentences.tr:
fa-law rahanūnī wa-ʿilmī maʿī * wa-kulli al-lifā tarwi al-miḥbarati
ʿalā qūti yawmin fa-rudda al-rihānu * wa-armū ilā al-qiṣṣati al-maqarrati
sentences.l:
So if they-pawned-me, with-my-knowledge with-me, * and all the-lifā you-quench the-inkwell,
for the-food of a-day, then let-be-returned the-pledge, * and throw-(you-all) to the-story the-abode.
sentences.i: Were they to pawn me, my learning with me and my inkwell too, for a single day's bread, the pledge would be handed back; and cast me off to my quiet resting-place.
sentences.n: This couplet is obscure and the text may be corrupt. وَكُلِّ اللِّفَا تَرْوِ الْمِحْبَرَةِ is kept as printed: اللِّفَا might be a form of لِفَافَة (wrappings), and تَرْوِ might be from رَوِيَ (to be quenched), but neither is certain, and the idiomatic English is a guess from the context, which says that the pawned man and his gear are worth less than a day's bread. The last words الْقِصَّةِ الْمَقَرَّةِ are also doubtful; القصة could be a misprint, and المقرة could be مَقَرّ, a dwelling-place. The vowels are supplied to make the rhyme -ra-ti.

sentences.t:
فَأَ مَّا الْفَقِيرُ وَحَالُ الْفَقِيرِ * وَعَيْشُ الْفَقِيرِ فَمَا أَكْدَرَهُ
وَفِى الصَّيْفِ يَعْجِزُ عَنْ قُوتِهِ * وَفِى الْبَرْدِ يَدْفِي عَلَى الْمِجْمَرَةِ
تَقُومُ عَلَيْهِ كِلَابُ الطَّرِيقِ * وَكُلُّ لَئِيمٍ بِذَا يَنْهَرُهُ
sentences.tr:
fa-ammā al-faqīru wa-ḥālu al-faqīri * wa-ʿaysh al-faqīri fa-mā akdarahu
wa-fī al-ṣayfi yaʿjizu ʿan qūtihi * wa-fī al-bardi yadfī ʿalā al-mijmarati
taqūmu ʿalayhi kilābu al-ṭarīqi * wa-kullu laʾīmin bi-dhā yanharuhu
sentences.l:
So as-for the-poor-man, and the-state of the-poor-man, * and the-life of the-poor-man, how murky-it!
And in the-summer he-is-unable (to reach) his-food, * and in the-cold he-warms-himself over the-brazier.
There-stand over-him the-dogs of the-road, * and every base-one for this rebukes-him.
sentences.i: As for the poor man, and the poor man's condition, and the poor man's life, how dark it is! In summer he cannot find his food, and in winter he must warm himself over a brazier. The dogs of the street set upon him, and every churl rebukes him for it.
sentences.n: The أَمَّا clause begins with the poor man as topic and the three lines that follow are all comment on him; the wording never rounds off into a single main clause, so read the lines as a list. يَدْفِي is written with yāʾ and reads as a colloquial verb dafiya "to be warm" (the Classical verb is دَفِئَ يَدْفَأُ). The final -hu of يَنْهَرُهُ is the rhyme. The pointing of the أَمَّا in the edition's two-word spelling فا ما is kept; read fa-ammā.

sentences.t:
إِذَا مَا شَكَى حَالَهُ لِامْرِئٍ * فَمَا فِي الْبَرِيَّةِ مَنْ يَعْذِرُهُ
إِذَا كَانَ هَذَا حَيَوةَ الْفَقِيرِ * فَأَصْلَحُ مَا كَانَ فِى الْمَقْبَرَةِ
sentences.tr:
idhā mā shakā ḥālahu li-imriʾin * fa-mā fī al-bariyyati man yaʿdhiruhu
idhā kāna hādhā ḥayawata al-faqīri * fa-aṣlaḥu mā kāna fī al-maqbarati
sentences.l:
If he-complains his-state to-a-man, * then there-is-not in the-creation one-who excuses-him.
If this is the-life of the-poor-man, * then the-most-fitting what there-is is in the-graveyard.
sentences.i: If he tells his plight to any man, there is no one in all creation who will pardon him. If this is the life of the poor, then the best thing there is lies in the graveyard.
sentences.n: شَكَى is written with alif maqṣūra (Classical شَكَا); the edition prints it so, and it is kept. حَيَوةَ is the older spelling of حَيَاةَ, kept as printed, and read ḥayāh. In هَذَا حَيَوةَ الْفَقِيرِ the second word is accusative as the predicate of كَانَ. الْبَرِيَّةِ is the created world, and the line rhymes on -ri-hi / -ra-ti.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْخَلِيفَةُ إِنْشَادَهُ قَالَ لِجَعْفَرٍ انْظُرْ هَذَا الرَّجُلَ الْفَقِيرَ وَانْظُرْ هَذَا الشِّعْرَ فَإِنَّهُ يَدُلُّ عَلَى أَحْبَابِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-khalīfatu inshādahu qāla li-Jaʿfarin unẓur hādhā al-rajula al-faqīra wa-unẓur hādhā al-shiʿra fa-innahu yadullu ʿalā aḥbābihi
sentences.l: So when the-caliph heard his-reciting, he-said to-Jaʿfar: look (at) this man the-poor, and look (at) this verse, for it points to his-loved-ones.
sentences.i: When the caliph heard his recitation he said to Jaʿfar: "Look at this poor man, and look at this poetry, for it bespeaks a man of breeding."
sentences.n: أَحْبَابِهِ ("his loved ones") is printed, but the sense wants a word like آدَابِهِ, "his good breeding", so the idiomatic English follows the sense; the printed word is what is vocalised. The verb انْظُرْ is repeated for emphasis, the second time governing الشِّعْرَ.

sentences.t: لَمْ الْخَلِيفَةُ سَلِّمْ إِلَيْهِ وَقُلْ لَهُ
sentences.tr: lam al-khalīfatu sallim ilayhi wa-qul lahu
sentences.l: Not the-caliph — greet to-him and say to-him:
sentences.i: Then the caliph said: "Greet him, and say to him:
sentences.n: لَمْ is printed where the sense requires ثُمَّ, "then": the vocalised text reads لَمْ, "not", but the sentence cannot be parsed that way, so read it as a misprint for ثم. The unstated "said to Jaʿfar" has to be supplied; سَلِّمْ إِلَيْهِ ("greet him", i.e. approach him courteously) is a command.

sentences.t: يَاشَيْخُ مَا صَنْعَتُكَ
sentences.tr: yā shaykhu mā ṣanʿatuka
sentences.l: O old-man, what (is) your-trade?
sentences.i: Old man, what is your trade?"
sentences.n: The edition runs يا and شيخ together, so it is written yāshaykh and read yā shaykh. صَنْعَةٌ (a craft, trade) is a Classical noun, though the usual word for a trade is صِنَاعَةٌ.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدِي أَنَا صَيَّادٌ وَعِنْدِى عِيلَةٌ وَخَرَجْتُ مِنْ بَيْتِي مِنْ نِصْفِ النَّهَارِ إِلَى هَذَا الْوَقْتِ لَمْ يَقْسِمِ اللَّهُ شَيْئًا أَقُوتُ بِهِ عِيَالِي وَقَدْ كَرِهْتُ نَفْسِي وَتَمَنَّيْتُ الْمَوْتَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā sayyidī anā ṣayyādun wa-ʿindī ʿīlatun wa-kharajtu min baytī min niṣfi al-nahāri ilā hādhā al-waqti lam yaqsimi Allāhu shayʾan aqūtu bihi ʿiyālī wa-qad karihtu nafsī wa-tamannaytu al-mawta
sentences.l: So he-said: O my-lord, I (am) a-fisher, and with-me (is) a-dependency, and I-went-out from my-house from the-middle of the-day to this time — not has-apportioned God anything I-sustain with-it my-dependents — and indeed I-have-loathed my-self and I-wished (for) the-death.
sentences.i: He said: "My lord, I am a fisherman, and I have a family. I left my house at midday and until this hour God has not allotted me a thing with which to feed my family. I have come to loathe myself, and have wished for death."
sentences.n: عِيلَةٌ is colloquial for a household of dependents (Classical عَيْلَةٌ means want, poverty, and would also suit the man's plight); it pairs with عِيَالِي, "my dependents". أَقُوتُ بِهِ is a relative clause on شَيْئًا with no linking word; بِـ in بِهِ marks the means, "with which". مِنْ نِصْفِ النَّهَارِ إِلَى هَذَا الْوَقْتِ, "from noon until now", is the bracket for the whole day's failure.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ تَرْجِعَ مَعَنَا الْبَحْرَ وَتَقِفَ عَلَى شَاطِئِ الدِّجْلَةِ وَتَرْمِيَ شَبَكَتَكَ عَلَى بَخْتِي وَمَهْمَا طَلَعَ أَشْتَرِيهِ مِنْكَ بِمِائَةِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu hal laka an tarjiʿa maʿanā al-baḥra wa-taqifa ʿalā shāṭiʾi al-Dijlati wa-tarmiya shabakataka ʿalā bakhtī wa-mahmā ṭalaʿa ashtarīhi minka bi-miʾati dīnārin
sentences.l: So the-caliph said: is-there for-you that you-return with-us (to) the-sea, and stand on the-bank of the-Tigris, and cast your-net on my-luck, and whatever comes-up I-buy-it from-you for a-hundred dinars?
sentences.i: The caliph said: "Would you come back with us to the river, stand on the bank of the Tigris and cast your net on my luck? Whatever comes up, I will buy it from you for a hundred dinars."
sentences.n: هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ is "is it for you to...?", the ordinary way of offering someone a chance. تَرْجِعَ مَعَنَا الْبَحْرَ puts the destination in the bare accusative, without إِلَى; that is a colloquial economy. The البحر here is the Tigris, as the next clause shows. After مَهْمَا ("whatever", a conditional) the apodosis has an indicative أَشْتَرِيهِ where the jussive would be Classical; this is Middle Arabic. عَلَى بَخْتِي, "on my luck", means at the Caliph's risk.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ لَمَّا سَمِعَ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ وَ قَٰلَ عَلَى رَأْسِي أَرْجِعُ مَعَكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa lammā samiʿa hādhā al-kalāma wa qāla ʿalā raʾsī arjiʿu maʿakum
sentences.l: So he-rejoiced when he-heard this speech, and he-said: on my-head — I-return with-you.
sentences.i: He rejoiced when he heard this and said: "On my head! I will go back with you."
sentences.n: The printed قل is a defective spelling for قال and carries the dagger alif here. It is written after a separate و because the line ends there, so it is وَ قَٰلَ, read wa-qāla. عَلَى رَأْسِي ("on my head") is the polite formula of glad compliance.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الصَّيَّادَ رَجَعَ مَعَهُمْ إِلَى الْبَحْرِ وَرَمَى شَبَكَتَهُ وَصَبَرَ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ṣayyāda rajaʿa maʿahum ilā al-baḥri wa-ramā shabakatahu wa-ṣabara ʿalayhā
sentences.l: Then indeed the-fisher returned with-them to the-sea, and cast his-net, and waited over-it.
sentences.i: Then the fisherman went back with them to the river, cast his net and waited over it.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ جَذَبَ الْخَيْطَ وَجَرَّ الشَّبَكَةَ إِلَيْهِ فَطَلَعَ فِى الشَّبَكَةِ صُنْدُوقٌ مَقْفُولٌ ثَقِيلُ الْوَزْنِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu jadhaba al-khayṭa wa-jarra al-shabakata ilayhi fa-ṭalaʿa fī al-shabakati ṣundūqun maqfūlun thaqīlu al-wazni
sentences.l: Then indeed-he pulled the-cord and dragged the-net to-him, and there-came-up in the-net a-chest locked, heavy of-weight.
sentences.i: Then he pulled the cord and dragged the net toward him, and up in the net came a locked chest, heavy in weight.
sentences.n: مَقْفُولٌ is the colloquial passive participle of قَفَلَ (Classical مُقْفَلٌ). ثَقِيلُ الْوَزْنِ is an adjective governing a following noun, "weighty in weight".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَهُ الْخَلِيفَةُ جَسَّهُ فَوَجَدَهُ ثَقِيلًا فَأَعْطَى لِلصَّيَّادِ مِائَةَ دِينَارٍ وَانْصَرَفَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓarahu al-khalīfatu jassahu fa-wajadahu thaqīlan fa-aʿṭā li-al-ṣayyādi miʾata dīnārin wa-inṣarafa
sentences.l: So when the-caliph looked-at-it he-felt-it, and he-found-it heavy, and he-gave to-the-fisher a-hundred dinars, and he-departed.
sentences.i: When the caliph saw it he felt it and found it heavy. He gave the fisherman his hundred dinars, and the man went his way.
sentences.n: أَعْطَى لِلصَّيَّادِ uses لِـ for the recipient, where Classical would give the recipient as a direct object; لِـ here marks the person to whom. The subject of وَانْصَرَفَ is the fisherman, not the Caliph, though the text does not say so.

sentences.t: وَحَمَلَ الصُّنْدُوقَ مَسْرُورٌ مَعَ الْخَلِيفَةِ وَطَلَعُوا بِهِ إِلَى الْقَصْرِ وَأَوْقَدُوا الشُّمُوعَ وَالصُّنْدُوقُ بَيْنَ يَدَيِ الْخَلِيفَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥamala al-ṣundūqa Masrūrun maʿa al-khalīfati wa-ṭalaʿū bihi ilā al-qaṣri wa-awqadū al-shumūʿa wa-al-ṣundūqu bayna yadayi al-khalīfati
sentences.l: And carried the-chest Masrūr with the-caliph, and they-went-up with-it to the-palace, and they-lit the-candles, while the-chest (was) between the-two-hands of the-caliph.
sentences.i: Masrūr carried the chest, and they went up with it, the caliph with them, to the palace, and lit the candles, and the chest was set before the caliph.
sentences.n: طَلَعُوا بِهِ, "they went up with it", uses بِـ to turn an intransitive verb into "take up". بَيْنَ يَدَيِ ("between the two hands of") is the standard idiom for "in front of".

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمَ جَعْفَرٌ وَمَسْرُورٌ وَكَسَرُوا الصُّنْدُوقَ فَوَجَدُوا فِيهِ قُفَّةَ خُوصٍ مَخِيطَةً بِخَيْطِ صُوفٍ أَحْمَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddama Jaʿfarun wa-Masrūrun wa-kasarū al-ṣundūqa fa-wajadū fīhi quffata khūṣin makhīṭatan bi-khayṭi ṣūfin aḥmara
sentences.l: So advanced Jaʿfar and Masrūr, and they-broke the-chest, and they-found in-it a-basket of-palm-leaf, sewn with-a-thread of wool red.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar and Masrūr stepped forward and broke open the chest, and found inside it a basket of palm-leaf, sewn shut with a thread of red wool.
sentences.n: The verb كَسَرُوا is plural because it covers both men, though the verb before it is singular with the first subject; this is normal. بِخَيْطِ صُوفٍ أَحْمَرَ: بِـ marks the instrument, "with", and أَحْمَرَ could agree with either خَيْطِ or صُوفٍ.

sentences.t: فَقَطَعُوا الْقُفَّةَ فَرَأَوْا فِيهَا فَرْدَةَ بِسَاطٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qaṭaʿū al-quffata fa-raʾaw fīhā fardata bisāṭin
sentences.l: So they-cut the-basket, and they-saw in-it a-piece of-carpet.
sentences.i: They cut the basket open and saw in it a piece of carpet.

sentences.t: فَشَالُوا الْفَرْدَةَ فَوَوَجَدُوا إِزَارًا وَجَدُوا فِيهِ صَبِيَّةً كَأَنَّهَا سَبِيكَةُ فِضَّةٍ مَقْتُولَةً مُقَطَّعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-shālū al-fardata fa-wa-wajadū izāran wajadū fīhi ṣabiyyatan ka-annahā sabīkatu fiḍḍatin maqtūlatan muqaṭṭaʿatan
sentences.l: So they-lifted the-piece, and-then-they-found a-wrap; they-found in-it a-girl, as-if-she (were) an-ingot of-silver, killed, cut-in-pieces.
sentences.i: They lifted the carpet and found a wrap, and in the wrap they found a young girl, gleaming like an ingot of silver, murdered and cut to pieces.
sentences.n: شَالُوا is colloquial (Egyptian شال, "to lift"); the Classical verb would be حَمَلُوا or رَفَعُوا. فووجدوا has a doubled waw that is probably a printer's error for فوجدوا; it is vocalised as printed, fa + wa + wajadū. إِزَارًا وَجَدُوا فِيهِ has no connective between the clauses: "a wrap; they found in it...". مَقْتُولَةً مُقَطَّعَةً are accusative circumstantial words on صَبِيَّةً. كَأَنَّهَا سَبِيكَةُ فِضَّةٍ: كَـ is not the preposition here; it is part of the particle كَأَنَّ, "as if".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَهَا الْخَلِيفَةُ تَأَسَّفَ وَجَرَتْ دُمُوعُهُ عَلَى خَدَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓarahā al-khalīfatu taʾassafa wa-jarat dumūʿuhu ʿalā khaddati
sentences.l: So when the-caliph looked-at-her he-grieved, and his-tears ran on his-cheek.
sentences.i: When the caliph looked at her he grieved, and the tears ran down his cheek.
sentences.n: خدة is printed with a tā marbūṭa where the sense wants a hāʾ (خَدِّهِ, "his cheek"). The letters are kept and vocalised as printed; the meaning is "his cheek".

sentences.t: وَالْتَفَتَ إِلَى جَعْفَرٍ وَقَالَ يَا كَلْبَ الْوُزَرَا تُقْتَلُ الْقَتْلَى فِي زَمَنِي وَيَرْمُوهُمْ فِى الْبَحْرِ وَيَصِيرُونَ مُتَعَلِّقِينَ بِذِمَّتِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-iltafata ilā Jaʿfarin wa-qāla yā kalba al-wuzarā tuqtalu al-qatlā fī zamanī wa-yarmūhum fī al-baḥri wa-yaṣīrūna mutaʿalliqīna bi-dhimmatī yawma al-qiyāmati
sentences.l: And he-turned to Jaʿfar and said: O dog of-the-viziers, are-killed the-slain in my-time, and they-throw-them into the-sea, and they-become clinging to-my-charge (on) the-Day of the-Resurrection?
sentences.i: He turned to Jaʿfar and said: "You dog among viziers! Are people slain in my time, and thrown into the river, to hang about my neck on the Day of Resurrection?"
sentences.n: الْوُزَرَا is printed without the final hamza of الوزراء; it is vocalised as printed. The sentence has no question particle, so it reads as an accusing question. تُقْتَلُ is pointed as passive (the slain are killed), agreeing in the feminine singular with the broken plural الْقَتْلَى. يَرْمُوهُمْ has lost the -na of the imperfect before the object suffix, a form non-Classical as printed; it means "they throw them". مُتَعَلِّقِينَ بِذِمَّتِي: بِـ goes with تَعَلَّقَ, "cling to"; ذِمَّة is the charge or responsibility.

sentences.t: وَاللَّهِ لَابُدَّ أَنْ آخُذَ حَقَّ هَذِهِ الصَّبِيَّةِ مِمَّنْ قَتَلَهَا وَلَأَ قْتُلَنَّهُ شَرَّ قَتْلَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-Allāhi lā budda an ākhudha ḥaqqa hādhihi al-ṣabiyyati mimman qatalahā wa-la-aqtulannahu sharra qatlatin
sentences.l: By-God, there-is-no escape that I-take the-right of this the-girl from-whoever killed-her, and I-shall-surely-kill-him (with) the-worst of-killings.
sentences.i: By God, I must exact justice for this girl from whoever killed her, and I will kill him by the most terrible of deaths.
sentences.n: لَابُدَّ is printed as one word. وَلَأ قْتُلَنَّهُ is printed with a space after the ولا, so read it as wa-la-aqtulannahu: the hamza-alif of أَقْتُلَنَّهُ was left at the end of the first word and the rest of the verb was split off. The lām is the oath lām, and the nūn of the emphatic -nna shows the oath. In the vocalisation the alif carries the hamza with fatḥa and the qāf carries the sukūn, so the pair reads together. شَرَّ قَتْلَةٍ is the cognate accusative, "the worst of killings".

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِجَعْفَرٍ وَ حَقِّ اتِّصَالِ نَسَبِى بِالْخَلِيفَةِ مِنْ بَنِي الْعَبَّاسِ إِنْ لَمْ تَأْتِنِي بِالَّذِى قَتَلَ هَذِهِ لِأُ نْصِفَهَا مِنْهُ شَنَقْتُكَ عَلَى بَابِ قَصْرِي وَأَرْبَعِينَ مِنْ بَنِي عَمِّكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla li-Jaʿfarin wa-ḥaqqi ittiṣāli nasabī bi-al-khalīfati min banī al-ʿAbbāsi in lam taʾtinī bi-alladhī qatala hādhihi li-unṣifahā minhu shanaqtuka ʿalā bābi qaṣrī wa-arbaʿīna min banī ʿammika
sentences.l: And he-said to-Jaʿfar: and by-the-right of the-connection of-my-lineage with-the-caliphs from the-sons of-al-ʿAbbās, if not you-bring-me the-one-who killed this (girl), that I-do-her-justice from-him, I-shall-hang you on the-door of-my-palace, and forty from the-sons of-your-uncle.
sentences.i: He said to Jaʿfar: "By the right of my line's kinship with the caliphs of the house of al-ʿAbbās, if you do not bring me the man who killed this girl, so that I may do her justice against him, I will hang you at the gate of my palace, and forty of your cousins with you."
sentences.n: The edition prints وَ حَقِّ with a space, the و of the oath standing at the end of a line; read wa-ḥaqqi. لا نصفها is printed as two words; it is read li-unṣifahā, the lām of purpose plus أُنْصِفَهَا, "that I may do her justice" (أَنْصَفَ, to deal fairly with): the lām's alif carries the hamza with ḍamma, and the nūn carries the sukūn. شَنَقْتُكَ is a perfect used as the apodosis of the conditional. اتِّصَالِ نَسَبِى: the Caliph swears by his own ties of blood. بَنِي عَمِّكَ, "the sons of your father's brother", are Jaʿfar's cousins, the Barmakids.

sentences.t: وَاغْتَاظَ الْخَلِيفَةُ غَيْظًا شَدِيدًا فَخَرَجَ جَعْفَرٌ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ightāẓa al-khalīfatu ghayẓan shadīdan fa-kharaja Jaʿfarun min bayni yadayhi wa-qāla lahu
sentences.l: And the caliph was-enraged, a severe rage, so Jaʿfar went-out from between his two hands, and said to him:
sentences.i: The caliph was seized with violent rage, and Jaʿfar went out from his presence and said to him:
sentences.n: مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ, "from between his two hands", is the ordinary idiom for "from his presence"; بَيْنَ يَدَيْ ("before") recurs throughout this night.

sentences.t: أَمْهِلْنِي ثَلَٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ
sentences.tr: amhilnī thalāthata ayyāmin
sentences.l: Grant-me-respite three days.
sentences.i: Give me three days' grace.
sentences.n: ثلثة is the edition's defective spelling of ثَلَاثَة; it is pointed with the dagger alif and read thalātha.

sentences.t: قَالَ أَمْهَلْتُكَ
sentences.tr: qāla amhaltuka
sentences.l: He said: I have-granted-you-respite.
sentences.i: He said, "I grant it."

sentences.t: فَنَزَلَ جَعْفَرٌ الْمَدِينَةَ وَهُوَ حَزِينٌ
sentences.tr: fa-nazala Jaʿfarun al-madīnata wa-huwa ḥazīnun
sentences.l: And Jaʿfar went-down (to) the city, and he (was) sorrowful.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar went down into the city, grieving.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ مِنْ أَيْنَ أَعْرِفُ مَنْ قَتَلَ هَٰذِهِ الصَّبِيَّةَ حَتَّى إِنِّي أُحْضِرَهُ لِلْخَلِيفَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla fī nafsihi min ayna aʿrifu man qatala hādhihi al-ṣabiyyata ḥattā innī uḥḍiruhu li-al-khalīfati
sentences.l: And he said in his self: From where do I know who killed this girl, so-that indeed I bring-him to the caliph,
sentences.i: And he said to himself, "How am I to learn who killed this girl, so that I may bring him to the caliph,
sentences.n: حَتَّى إِنِّي أُحْضِرُهُ is not Classical (حَتَّى would take a bare subjunctive, أُحْضِرَهُ); it is pointed as the text has it, with the indicative. The printed اني could also be read أَنِّي; the sense is the same.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ أَحْضَرْتُ لَهُ غَيْرَهُ يَصِيرُ مُتَعَلِّقًا فِي ذِمَّتِي وَلَا أَدْرِي مَا أَمْنَعُ
sentences.tr: wa-in aḥḍartu lahu ghayrahu yaṣīru mutaʿalliqan fī dhimmatī wa-lā adrī mā amnaʿu
sentences.l: and if I bring to-him someone-other-than-him, it becomes hanging in my obligation, and I do-not know what I (can) ward-off.
sentences.i: and if I bring him someone else, it will hang upon my conscience, and I do not know what defence to make."
sentences.n: Two Middle Arabic features: the result clause يَصِيرُ has no فَ after the وَإِنْ condition, and مَا أَمْنَعُ is obscure. أَمْنَعُ is pointed as "I ward off / prevent" (Lane, منع), giving roughly "what I can do to fend it off"; the sense is a guess.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ جَعْفَرًا جَلَسَ فِي بَيْتِهِ ثَلَٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ وَفِى الْيَوْمِ الرَّابِعِ أَرْسَلَ الْخَلِيفَةُ وَرَاءَهُ بَعْضَ الْحُجَّابِ يَطْلُبُهُ فَطَلَعَ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna Jaʿfaran jalasa fī baytihi thalāthata ayyāmin wa-fī al-yawmi al-rābiʿi arsala al-khalīfatu warāʾahu baʿḍa al-ḥujjābi yaṭlubuhu fa-ṭalaʿa ilayhi
sentences.l: Then indeed Jaʿfar sat in his house three days, and on the fourth day the caliph sent behind-him some (of) the chamberlains, seeking him; so he went-up to him.
sentences.i: Then Jaʿfar stayed in his house three days, and on the fourth day the caliph sent some of the chamberlains after him to summon him, and he went up to the caliph.
sentences.n: طَلَعَ إِلَيْهِ, "went up to him", is the everyday word for going up to a palace or a superior. The edition prints فى with ى here; the pointing follows it.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ لَهُ أَيْنَ قَاتِلُ الصَّبِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu lahu ayna qātilu al-ṣabiyyati
sentences.l: And the caliph said to him: Where (is) the killer of the girl?
sentences.i: The caliph said to him, "Where is the girl's killer?"

sentences.t: قَالَ جَعْفَرٌ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنَا كُنْتُ عَرِيفَ الْقَتْلَى حَتَّى أَعْرِفَ قَاتِلَهَا
sentences.tr: qāla Jaʿfarun yā amīra al-muʾminīna anā kuntu ʿarīfa al-qatlā ḥattā aʿrifa qātilahā
sentences.l: Jaʿfar said: O Commander of-the-Faithful, I was (the) overseer of-the-slain, so-that I might-know her killer.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar said, "Commander of the Faithful, am I the overseer of the murdered, that I should know her killer?"
sentences.n: As printed this is a statement, "I was the overseer of the slain"; the idiomatic layer reads it as Jaʿfar's bitter rhetorical question (the intonation carries it, since there is no particle). عَرِيف is a headman or officer in charge of a group (Lane).

sentences.t: فَاغْتَاظَ الْخَلِيفَةُ وَأَمَرَ بِشَنْقِهِ تَحْتَ قَصْرِهِ وَأَمَرَ مُنَادِيًا يُنَادِي فِي شَوَارِعِ بَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: fa-ightāẓa al-khalīfatu wa-amara bi-shanqihi taḥta qaṣrihi wa-amara munādiyan yunādī fī shawāriʿi Baghdāda
sentences.l: And the caliph was-enraged, and ordered the hanging of-him beneath his palace, and ordered a crier to-call in the streets of Baghdad:
sentences.i: The caliph flew into a rage and ordered him hanged beneath his palace, and commanded a crier to proclaim through the streets of Baghdad:
sentences.n: أَمَرَ بِـ, "command (something)", takes بِ; the second أَمَرَ takes the crier as its object and the following verb without أَنْ, a construction the text prefers.

sentences.t: مَنْ أَرَادَ الْفُرْجَةَ عَلَى شَنْقِ جَعْفَرٍ الْبَرْمَكِيِّ وَزِيرِ الْخَلِيفَةِ وَشَنْقِ أَرْبَعِينَ بَرْمَكِيًّا مِنْ أَوْلَادِ عَمِّهِ عَلَى بَابِ قَصْرِ الْخَلِيفَةِ فَلْيَخْرُجْ يَتَفَرَّجْ
sentences.tr: man arāda al-furjata ʿalā shanqi Jaʿfarin al-Barmakiyyi wazīri al-khalīfati wa-shanqi arbaʿīna Barmakiyyan min awlādi ʿammihi ʿalā bābi qaṣri al-khalīfati fa-li-yakhruj yatafarraj
sentences.l: Whoever wanted the spectacle upon the hanging of Jaʿfar the Barmakid, vizier of-the-caliph, and the hanging of forty Barmakids from the sons of his paternal-uncle, at the gate of the palace of-the-caliph, let-him go-out (and) watch.
sentences.i: Whoever wishes to see the sight of the hanging of Jaʿfar the Barmecide, the caliph's vizier, and of forty Barmecides of his cousins, at the gate of the caliph's palace, let him come out and watch.
sentences.n: أَوْلَادِ عَمِّهِ, "sons of his paternal uncle", means his cousins on the father's side, though here it stands for his wider kin. The command فَلْيَخْرُجْ يَتَفَرَّجْ is a jussive with a second jussive following it directly ("let him go out, watch").

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَتِ النَّاسُ مِنْ جَمِيعِ الْحَارَاتِ يَتَفَرَّجُونَ عَلَى شَنْقِ جَعْفَرٍ وَأَوْلَادِ عَمِّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-kharajati al-nāsu min jamīʿi al-ḥārāti yatafarrajūna ʿalā shanqi Jaʿfarin wa-awlādi ʿammihi
sentences.l: And the people (she-went-out) went-out from all the quarters, watching upon the hanging of Jaʿfar and the sons of his uncle.
sentences.i: So the people came out from every quarter, to watch the hanging of Jaʿfar and his cousins.
sentences.n: فَخَرَجَتِ النَّاسُ has a feminine singular verb with the collective النَّاس, as in colloquial usage and, less often, in Classical Arabic. الْحَارَات (sing. حَارَة) is the colloquial word for city quarters.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا سَبَبَ شَنْقِهِمْ وَنَصَبُوا الْخَشَبَ وَأَوْقَفُوهُمْ تَحْتَهُ لِأَجْلِ الشَّنْقِ وَصَارُوا يَنْتَظِرُونَ الْإِذْنَ مِنَ الْخَلِيفَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yaʿlamū sababa shanqihim wa-naṣabū al-khashaba wa-awqafūhum taḥtahu li-ajli al-shanqi wa-ṣārū yantaẓirūna al-idhna mina al-khalīfati
sentences.l: And they did-not know the cause of their hanging, and they set-up the wood, and made-them-stand beneath it for the sake of the hanging, and began awaiting the permission from the caliph.
sentences.i: They did not know why the men were to be hanged. The gallows were set up and the condemned were stood beneath them for the hanging, and the executioners began to wait for the caliph's leave.
sentences.n: نَصَبُوا الْخَشَبَ, "they set up the timber", is the gallows. The subject of the plural verbs shifts without warning from the onlookers to the executioners.

sentences.t: وَكَانَتِ الْإِشَارَةُ هَكَذَا
sentences.tr: wa-kānati al-ishāratu hākadhā
sentences.l: And the sign was thus.
sentences.i: And such was the signal.
sentences.n: The line is compressed: the caliph's signal was the awaited cue, and the next clause returns to the crowd. The idiomatic rendering supplies what هَكَذَا ("thus") points at; a plainer reading is "and such was the signal (agreed)."

sentences.t: وَصَارَ الْخَلْقُ يَتَبَاكَوْنَ عَلَى جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَوْلَادِ عَمِّهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra al-khalqu yatabākawna ʿalā Jaʿfarin wa-awlādi ʿammihi
sentences.l: And the creation began weeping-together over Jaʿfar and the sons of his uncle.
sentences.i: And the crowd began to weep for Jaʿfar and his cousins.
sentences.n: يَتَبَاكَوْنَ is Form VI, which in Lane can mean "to feign weeping" but here plainly means that they wept, one taking the cue from another. الْخَلْق, "the creation", is the ordinary word for "the crowd".

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ كَذَٰلِكَ وَإِذَا بِشَابٍّ حَسَنِ الْوَجْهِ نَقِيِّ الْأَثْوَابِ بِوَجْهٍ أَقْمَرَ وَطَرْفٍ أَحْوَرَ وَجَبِينٍ أَزْهَرَ وَخَدٍّ أَحْمَرَ وَعِذَارٍ أَخْضَرَ وَشَامَةٍ كَأَنَّهُ قُرْصُ عَنْبَرٍ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā hum ka-dhālika wa-idhā bi-shābbin ḥasani al-wajhi naqiyyi al-athwābi bi-wajhin aqmara wa-ṭarfin aḥwara wa-jabīnin azhara wa-khaddin aḥmara wa-ʿidhārin akhḍara wa-shāmatin ka-annahu qurṣu ʿanbarin
sentences.l: So while they (were) like-that, and behold, with a youth handsome-of-face, clean-of-garments, with a face moon-bright, and an eye wide-and-dark, and a brow shining, and a cheek red, and a down-of-the-cheek green, and a mole as-if-it (were) a disc of ambergris.
sentences.i: While they were thus, behold, a youth appeared, fair of face and clean of raiment: his face moon-bright, his eye dark and wide, his brow shining, his cheek rosy, the down on his cheek dark green, and a mole like a disc of ambergris.
sentences.n: This is a set piece of sajʿ, the adjectives all closing in -ar: أَقْمَرَ / أَحْوَرَ / أَزْهَرَ / أَحْمَرَ / أَخْضَرَ. The بِ of وَإِذَا بِشَابٍّ only marks what appears, and the later بِوَجْهٍ, وَطَرْفٍ … continue in the genitive after it, giving "with a face …". أَخْضَر, "green", of down on the cheek means dark. The pronoun of كَأَنَّهُ is masculine although شَامَة is feminine; it is kept as printed (with the archive's own precomposed hamza), and the sense is "like a disc of ambergris".

sentences.t: وَمَازَالَ يَفْسَحُ النَّاسَ إِلَى أَنْ وَقَفَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ جَعْفَرٍ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zāla yafsaḥu al-nāsa ilā an waqafa bayna yaday Jaʿfarin
sentences.l: And he did-not cease making-room (among) the people until he stood between the two hands of Jaʿfar.
sentences.i: And he kept making way through the people until he stood before Jaʿfar.
sentences.n: The edition joins وَمَازَالَ into one word; it is pointed as the negative verb مَا زَالَ, "kept on".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ سَلَامَتَكَ مِنْ هَٰذِهِ الْوَقْفَةِ يَا سَيِّدَ الْأُمَرَاءِ وَكَهْفَ الْفُقَرَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu salāmataka min hādhihi al-waqfati yā sayyida al-umarāʾi wa-kahfa al-fuqarāʾi
sentences.l: And he said to him: Your safety from this standing, O lord of-the-commanders and cave of-the-poor!
sentences.i: He said to him, "Peace be with you, and may you be safe from this ordeal, O lord of emirs and refuge of the poor!"
sentences.n: سَلَامَتَكَ is a greeting in the accusative, an elliptical wish: "(I wish) your safety". الْوَقْفَة is the standing at the gallows. The rhymed pair الْأُمَرَاءِ / الْفُقَرَاءِ is sajʿ, and كَهْف, "cave", is a shelter.

sentences.t: الَّذِي قَتَلَ الْقَتِيلَةَ الَّتِي وَجَدْتُمُوهَا فِى الصُّنْدُوقِ أَنَافَاشْنُقْنِي عَنْهَا وَخُذْ حَقَّهَا مِنِّي
sentences.tr: alladhī qatala al-qatīlata allatī wajadtumūhā fī al-ṣundūqi anā fa-ishnuqnī ʿanhā wa-khudh ḥaqqahā minnī
sentences.l: The one-who killed the slain-woman whom you-found in the chest (is) I; so hang me for her, and take her right from me.
sentences.i: It is I who killed the murdered woman you found in the chest. Hang me for her, and take her due from me.
sentences.n: The edition prints أنا and فاشنقني run together as one word, أَنَافَاشْنُقْنِي; it is pointed as أَنَا فَاشْنُقْنِي and kept joined. The predicate أَنَا comes last: "the one who killed … (is) I".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ جَعْفَرٌ كَلَامَ الشَّابِّ وَمَا أَبْدَاهُ مِنَ الْخِطَابِ فَرِحَ بِخَلَاصِ نَفْسِهِ وَحَزِنَ عَلَى الشَّابِّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Jaʿfarun kalāma al-shābbi wa-mā abdāhu mina al-khiṭābi fariḥa bi-khalāṣi nafsihi wa-ḥazina ʿalā al-shābbi
sentences.l: And when Jaʿfar heard the speech of-the-youth and what he-showed of the address, he-rejoiced at the deliverance of his self and grieved over the youth.
sentences.i: When Jaʿfar heard the youth's words and the speech he had made, he rejoiced that he himself was delivered, and grieved for the youth.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ فِى الْكَلَامِ وَإِذَا بِشَيْخٍ كَبِيرٍ طَاعِنٍ فِى السِّنِّ يَفْسَحُ النَّاسَ وَيَشُقُّ بَيْنَ الْخَلَائِقِ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلَ إِلَى جَعْفَرٍ وَالشَّابِّ فَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā hum fī al-kalāmi wa-idhā bi-shaykhin kabīrin ṭāʿinin fī al-sinni yafsaḥu al-nāsa wa-yashuqqu bayna al-khalāʾiqi ilā an waṣala ilā Jaʿfarin wa-al-shābbi fa-sallama ʿalayhimā
sentences.l: So while they (were) in the talk, and behold, with an old-man, great, piercing into age, making-room (among) the people and splitting between the creatures, until he reached Jaʿfar and the youth, and greeted them both.
sentences.i: While they were talking, behold, a great old man, far advanced in years, was making way through the people and cleaving through the throng, until he reached Jaʿfar and the youth and greeted them both.
sentences.n: طَاعِنٌ فِى السِّنِّ, "piercing into age", is Lane's طَعَنَ فِى السِّنِّ, "to be advanced in years". الْخَلَائِق, "the creatures", is again the crowd. The edition prints ئ precomposed in this word.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَيُّهَا الْوَزِيرُ وَالسَّيِّدُ الْخَطِيرُ لَا تُصَدِّقْ كَلَامَ هَٰذَا الشَّابِّ فِيمَا يَقُولُ فَإِنَّهُ مَا قَتَلَ الصَّبِيَّةَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَخُذْ حَقَّهَا مِنِّي أَوْ أُطَالِبُكَ بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى إِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ayyuhā al-wazīru wa-al-sayyidu al-khaṭīru lā tuṣaddiq kalāma hādhā al-shābbi fīmā yaqūlu fa-innahu mā qatala al-ṣabiyyata illā anā fa-khudh ḥaqqahā minnī aw uṭālibuka bayna yaday Allāhi taʿālā in lam tafʿal
sentences.l: And he said: O you the vizier and the lord, the eminent, do-not believe the speech of this youth in what he says, for indeed-he did-not kill the girl except I; so take her right from me, or I (shall) demand-of-you between the hands of God, Exalted, if you do-not.
sentences.i: He said, "O vizier, O lord of high estate, do not believe what this youth says, for none killed the girl but I. So take her due from me, or I shall call you to account before God Most High, if you do not."
sentences.n: أَوْ أُطَالِبُكَ has the indicative, where a Classical writer would use the subjunctive after أَوْ meaning "or else". The pair الْوَزِيرُ / الْخَطِيرُ rhymes. بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ, "between the hands of God", is "before God", at the Judgment.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّابُّ أَيُّهَا الْوَزِيرُ هَٰذَا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ خَرْفَانُ لَا يَدْرِي مَا يَقُولُ وَأَنَا الَّذِي قَتَلْتُهَا فَخُذْ حَقَّهَا مِنِّي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shābbu ayyuhā al-wazīru hādhā shaykhun kabīrun kharfānu lā yadrī mā yaqūlu wa-anā alladhī qataltuhā fa-khudh ḥaqqahā minnī
sentences.l: And the youth said: O vizier, this (is) an old-man, great, senile, he does-not know what he says, and I (am) the one-who killed her; so take her right from me.
sentences.i: The youth said, "O vizier, this is a doddering old man who does not know what he says. It was I who killed her; take her due from me."
sentences.n: خَرْفَانُ is the colloquial adjective for senile (Classical would be خَرِفٌ, Lane خَرِفَ "became disordered in mind through age"); it is pointed as an invariable predicate, and the form is somewhat uncertain.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّيْخُ يَا وَلَدِي أَنْتَ صَغِيرٌ تَشْتَهِي الدُّنْيَا وَأَنَا كَبِيرٌ شَبِعْتُ مِنَ الدُّنْيَا وَأَنَا أَفْدِيكَ بِرُوحِي وَأَفْدِي الْوَزِيرَ وَبَنِي عَمِّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shaykhu yā waladī anta ṣaghīrun tashtahī al-dunyā wa-anā kabīrun shabiʿtu mina al-dunyā wa-anā afdīka bi-rūḥī wa-afdī al-wazīra wa-banī ʿammihi
sentences.l: And the old-man said: O my son, you (are) small, you desire the world, and I (am) great, I-have-had-my-fill from the world, and I ransom-you with my soul, and I ransom the vizier and the sons of his uncle.
sentences.i: The old man said, "My son, you are young and still crave the world, while I am old and have had my fill of it. I will ransom you with my life, and ransom the vizier and his cousins as well,
sentences.n: صَغِير and كَبِير, "small" and "great", stand for young and old. أَفْدِيكَ بِرُوحِي, "I ransom you with my soul", is a stock phrase of devotion.

sentences.t: وَ مَا قَتَلَ الصَّبِيَّةَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَبِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ عَجِّلْ بِشَنْقِي فَلَا حَيَوٰةَ لِي بَعْدَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-mā qatala al-ṣabiyyata illā anā fa-bi-Allāhi ʿalayka ʿajjil bi-shanqī fa-lā ḥayāta lī baʿdahā
sentences.l: and none killed the girl except I; so by God upon you, hasten with my hanging, for (there is) no life for me after her.
sentences.i: for none killed the girl but I. So, for God's sake, I beg you, make haste to hang me, for there is no life for me after her."
sentences.n: حَيَوٰة is the older spelling with wāw, kept as printed and read ḥayāh. فَبِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ, "by God upon you", is an oath of entreaty. عَجِّلْ بِـ, "hasten with", takes بِ.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ الْوَزِيرُ إِلَى ذَلِكَ تَعَجَّبَ وَأَخَذَ الشَّابَّ وَالشَّيْخَ وَطَلَعَ بِهِمَا إِلَى الْخَلِيفَةِ وَقَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ وَقَالَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓara al-wazīru ilā dhālika taʿajjaba wa-akhadha al-shābba wa-al-shaykha wa-ṭalaʿa bihimā ilā al-khalīfati wa-qabbala al-arḍa wa-qāla
sentences.l: And when the vizier looked at that, he marvelled, and took the youth and the old man, and went-up with the two-of-them to the caliph, and kissed the ground, and said.
sentences.i: When the vizier saw this he was amazed. He took the young man and the old man, went up with them to the caliph, kissed the ground, and said:
sentences.n: قَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ, "kissed the ground," is the courtly gesture of approaching a ruler. بِهِمَا is the dual: the vizier brings the two men up together.

sentences.t: يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ قَدْ أَحْضَرْنَا قَاتِلَ الصَّبِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: yā amīra al-muʾminīna qad aḥḍarnā qātila al-ṣabiyyati
sentences.l: O commander of the Faithful, we have brought the slayer of the girl.
sentences.i: Commander of the Faithful, we have brought the killer of the girl.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ أَيْنَ هُوَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu ayna huwa
sentences.l: And the caliph said: Where is he?

sentences.t: فَقَالَ إِنَّ هَذَا الشَّابَّ يَقُولُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْقَاتِلُ وَ هَذَا الشَّيْخُ يُكَذِّبُهُ وَيَقُولُ هُوَ الْقَاتِلُ وَهَا هُمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla inna hādhā al-shābba yaqūlu innahu huwa al-qātilu wa-hādhā al-shaykhu yukadhdhibuhu wa-yaqūlu huwa al-qātilu wa-hā humā bayna yadayka
sentences.l: And he said: Indeed this youth says that he, he is the slayer, and this elder calls-him-a-liar and says he is the slayer; and here they-two are, between your two-hands.
sentences.i: He said: This young man says that he is the killer, and this old man calls him a liar and says that he is the killer. Here they both are before you.
sentences.n: بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ, "between your two hands," is the standard idiom for "in your presence."

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ الْخَلِيفَةُ إِلَى الشَّيْخِ وَالشَّابِّ وَقَالَ مَنْ فِيكُمْ قَتَلَ هَذِهِ الصَّبِيَّةَ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara al-khalīfatu ilā al-shaykhi wa-al-shābbi wa-qāla man fīkum qatala hādhihi al-ṣabiyyata
sentences.l: And the caliph looked at the old man and the youth and said: Who among you killed this girl?
sentences.i: The caliph looked at the old man and the young man and said: Which of you killed this girl?

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّابُّ أَنَا وَقَالَ الشَّيْخُ مَا قَتَلَهَا إِلَّا أَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shābbu anā wa-qāla al-shaykhu mā qatalahā illā anā
sentences.l: And the youth said: I. And the old man said: None killed her but I.
sentences.i: The young man said, "I." And the old man said, "No one killed her but I."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ لِجَعْفَرَ خُذِ الِاثْنَيْنِ وَاشْنُقْهُمَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu li-Jaʿfara khudhi al-ithnayni wa-ushnuqhumā
sentences.l: And the caliph said to Jaʿfar: Take the two and hang-them-both.
sentences.i: The caliph said to Jaʿfar: Take the two of them and hang them.
sentences.n: لِجَعْفَرَ: the lām is the preposition "to" after قَالَ; Jaʿfar is a diptote, hence the fatḥa in the genitive.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ جَعْفَرُ إِذَا كَانَ أَحَدُهُمَا قَتَلَ فَشَنْقُ الثَّانِي ظُلْمٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Jaʿfaru idhā kāna aḥaduhumā qatala fa-shanqu al-thānī ẓulmun
sentences.l: And Jaʿfar said: If one-of-the-two killed, then the hanging of the second is a wrong.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar said: If only one of them killed her, then to hang the other is an injustice.
sentences.n: The edition prints فشنق; I read it as the verbal noun شَنْق "hanging" (the apodosis is a nominal sentence with ظُلْمٌ). Reading it as a verb, فَشَنَقَ, would leave ظلم without a subject.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّابُّ وَحَقِّ مَنْ رَفَعَ السَّمَاءَ وَبَسَطَ الْأَرْضَ أَنَا الَّذِي قَتَلْتُ الصَّبِيَّةَ وَأَدَّى أَمَارَةَ قِتْلَتِهَا وَوَصَفَ مَا وَجَدَهُ الْخَلِيفَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shābbu wa-ḥaqqi man rafaʿa al-samāʾa wa-basaṭa al-arḍa anā alladhī qataltu al-ṣabiyyata wa-addā amārata qitlatihā wa-waṣafa mā wajadahu al-khalīfatu
sentences.l: And the youth said: By the right of Him-who raised the sky and spread the earth, I am the-one-who killed the girl. And he delivered the sign of her manner-of-killing, and described what the caliph had found.
sentences.i: The young man said: By the right of Him who raised the heavens and spread the earth, I am the one who killed the girl. And he gave the tokens of how he had killed her, and described what the caliph had found.
sentences.n: The edition prints قتلتها after امارة. I read أَمَارَةَ قِتْلَتِهَا, "the token of the manner of her killing"; the alternative, أَمَارَةً قَتَلْتُهَا "a token: I killed her," does not suit the third-person narration that surrounds it. وَحَقِّ مَنْ ... is an oath: wāw of oath + genitive.

sentences.t: فَتَحَقَّقَ عِنْدَ الْخَلِيفَةِ أَنَّ الشَّابَّ هُوَ الَّذِي قَتَلَ الصَّبِيَّةَ فَتَعَجَّبَ الْخَلِيفَةُ مِنْ قِصَّتِهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-taḥaqqaqa ʿinda al-khalīfati anna al-shābba huwa alladhī qatala al-ṣabiyyata fa-taʿajjaba al-khalīfatu min qiṣṣatihimā
sentences.l: And it became-certain in-the-presence-of the caliph that the youth was the-one-who killed the girl, and the caliph marvelled at their-two story.
sentences.i: It was established in the caliph's mind that the young man was the one who had killed the girl, and the caliph marvelled at the story of the two of them.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ مَا سَبَبُ قَتْلِكَ لِهَذِهِ الصَّبِيَّةِ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَأَيْشْ سَبَبُ إِقْرَارِكَ بِالْقَتْلِ مِنْ غَيْرِ ضَرْبٍ وَمَجِيئِكَ بِنَفْسِكَ فِي هَذَا وَتَقُولُ خُذُوا حَقَّهَا مِنِّي
sentences.tr: wa-qāla mā sababu qatlika li-hādhihi al-ṣabiyyati bi-ghayri ḥaqqin wa-aysh sababu iqrārika bi-al-qatli min ghayri ḍarbin wa-majīʾika bi-nafsika fī hādhā wa-taqūlu khudhū ḥaqqahā minnī
sentences.l: And he said: What is the cause of your killing of this girl without right, and what (is) the cause of your confessing to the killing without beating, and your coming by your-self into this, and you say: Take her right from me?
sentences.i: He said: What made you kill this girl without right? And why did you confess to the killing without being beaten, and come of your own accord into this, saying, "Take her due from me"?
sentences.n: وَأَيْشْ is colloquial, a contraction of أَيُّ شَيْءٍ "what thing?" (compare Egyptian ēsh), so "what?" or "why?" here. لِهَذِهِ: the lām marks the object of the verbal noun قَتْلِكَ ("your killing of ..."). بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ, "without right," is the standard legal phrase for wrongful killing.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّابُّ اعْلَمْ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنَّ هَذِهِ الصَّبِيَّةَ زَوْجَتِي وَ بِنْتُ عَمِّي وَهَذَا الشَّيْخُ أَبُوهَا وَهُوَ عَمِّي وَتَزَوَّجْتُ بِهَا وَهِيَ بِكْرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shābbu iʿlam yā amīra al-muʾminīna anna hādhihi al-ṣabiyyata zawjatī wa-bintu ʿammī wa-hādhā al-shaykhu abūhā wa-huwa ʿammī wa-tazawwajtu bihā wa-hiya bikrun
sentences.l: And the youth said: Know, O commander of the Faithful, that this girl is my wife and the daughter of my paternal-uncle, and this elder is her father, and he is my paternal-uncle; and I married her, and she (was) a virgin.
sentences.i: The young man said: Know, Commander of the Faithful, that this girl was my wife and my cousin, the daughter of my father's brother, and that this old man is her father and my uncle. I married her when she was a virgin.
sentences.n: The formula اعْلَمْ يَا أَمِيرَ ... أَنَّ, "know, O ..., that ...," introduces a narrative addressed to a ruler. بنت عمي, "daughter of my paternal uncle," is the normal Arabic for a cousin of this kind, and marriage to her was the preferred match. In تَزَوَّجْتُ بِهَا the bi- is a Middle Arabic extra, where Classical would take the direct object.

sentences.t: فَرَزَقَنِي اللَّهُ مِنْهَا ثَلَٰثَةَ أَوْلَادٍ ذُكُورٍ وَكَانَتْ تُحِبُّنِي وَتَخْدُمُنِي وَ لَمْ أَرَ عَلَيْهَا سُوءًا وَكُنْتُ أَنَا أَيْضًا أُحِبُّهَا حُبًّا عَظِيمًا
sentences.tr: fa-razaqanī Allāhu minhā thalāthata awlādin dhukūrin wa-kānat tuḥibbunī wa-takhdumunī wa-lam ara ʿalayhā sūʾan wa-kuntu anā ayḍan uḥibbuhā ḥubban ʿaẓīman
sentences.l: And God provided-me from her three children, males; and she used-to love me and serve me, and I did not see against her any evil; and I too loved her, a great love.
sentences.i: God gave me three sons by her. She loved me and served me, and I saw no ill in her, and I, for my part, loved her with a great love.
sentences.n: ثلثة is printed without the alif, a defective spelling; it is pointed here with the dagger alif (thalāthah). ثَلَٰثَةَ أَوْلَادٍ ذُكُورٍ is "three children, males," with the number in apposition to a plural of the noun.

sentences.t: إِلَى أَنْ كَانَ أَوَّلُ هَذَا الشَّهْرِ فَمَرِضَتْ مَرَضًا شَدِيدًا فَأَحْضَرْتُ لَهَا الْأَطِبَّاءَ فَتَوَجَّهَتْ لَهَا الْعَافِيَةُ قَلِيلًا قَلِيلًا
sentences.tr: ilā an kāna awwalu hādhā al-shahri fa-mariḍat maraḍan shadīdan fa-aḥḍartu lahā al-aṭibbāʾa fa-tawajjahat lahā al-ʿāfiyatu qalīlan qalīlan
sentences.l: Until it was the beginning of this month; and she fell-ill, a severe illness; and I brought for her the physicians, and health turned toward her, little by little.
sentences.i: Until, at the beginning of this month, she fell gravely ill. I brought physicians to her, and health gradually returned to her.
sentences.n: قَلِيلًا قَلِيلًا, repetition of a word, gives the sense "little by little."
