sentences.t: فَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ أُدْخِلَهَا الْحَمَّامَ فَقَالَتْ إِنِّي أُرِيدُ شَيْئًا قَبْلَ دُخُولِ الْحَمَّامِ فَقَدِ اشْتَهَيْتُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-aradtu an udkhilahā al-ḥammāma fa-qālat innī urīdu shayʾan qabla dukhūli al-ḥammāmi fa-qadi ishtahaytuhu
sentences.l: And I wanted to make-her-enter the bath; and she said: Indeed I want something before the entering of the bath, for I have craved it.
sentences.i: I wished to take her to the bath, but she said: I want something before I go into the bath, for I have a craving for it.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً وَمَا هُوَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan wa-mā huwa
sentences.l: And I said to her: Hearing and obedience! And what is it?
sentences.i: I said to her: With hearing and obedience; and what is it?
sentences.n: سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً is an accusative of the verb left unspoken ("I give you hearing and obedience"), the standard courteous assent.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ إِنِّي أَشْتَهِى تُفَّاحَةً أَشُمُّهَا وَأَعَضُّ مِنْهَا عَضَّةً
sentences.tr: fa-qālat innī ashtahī tuffāḥatan ashummuhā wa-aʿaḍḍu minhā ʿaḍḍatan
sentences.l: And she said: Indeed I crave an apple; I smell it and bite from it a bite.
sentences.i: She said: I crave an apple, that I may smell it and take a bite of it.
sentences.n: أَشْتَهِى is spelled with final ى (as often in this edition) and read ashtahī. أَشُمُّهَا وَأَعَضُّ are present tenses standing for a purpose clause ("that I may smell ... and bite"), with no أَنْ.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلْتُ مِنْ سَاعَتِي الْمَدِينَةَ وَفَتَّشْتُ عَلَى التُّفَّاحِ فَلَمْ أَجِدْهُ وَلَوْ كَانَتِ الْوَاحِدَةُ بِدِينَارٍ لَاشْتَرَيْتُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-dakhaltu min sāʿatī al-madīnata wa-fattashtu ʿalā al-tuffāḥi fa-lam ajidhu wa-law kānati al-wāḥidatu bi-dīnārin la-ishtaraytuhā
sentences.l: And I entered, from my hour, the city, and searched for apples, and did not find them; and had the one been for a dinar, I would have bought it.
sentences.i: I went into the city at once and searched for apples, but I could not find any; had a single apple cost a dinar, I would have bought it.
sentences.n: مِنْ سَاعَتِي, "from my hour," means "that very moment." The lām of لَاشْتَرَيْتُهَا answers لَوْ. The edition writes the two words joined.

sentences.t: فَشَقَّ عَلَىَّ ذَلِكَ وَطَلَعْتُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقُلْتُ لَهَا يَابِنْتَ عَمِّي وَاللَّهِ مَالَقِيتُ شَيْئًا
sentences.tr: fa-shaqqa ʿalayya dhālika wa-ṭalaʿtu ilā al-bayti wa-qultu lahā yā bint ʿammī wa-Allāhi mā laqītu shayʾan
sentences.l: And that was hard upon me, and I went-up to the house and said to her: O daughter of my uncle, by God, I found nothing.
sentences.i: This distressed me. I went up to the house and said to her: Cousin, by God, I found nothing.
sentences.n: The edition prints عَلَىَّ with ى for عَلَيَّ, and joins يَابِنْتَ and مَالَقِيتُ. In يَا بِنْتَ عَمِّي the noun after يَا is accusative because it is in construct. وَاللَّهِ is the wāw of oath, with the divine name in the genitive.

sentences.t: فَتَشَوَّشْتُ وَهِيَ ضَعِيفَةٌ وَزَادَ عَلَيْهَا الضَّعْفُ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ كَثِيرًا فَبِتُّ وَأَنَا مُتَفَكِّرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-tashawwashtu wa-hiya ḍaʿīfatun wa-zāda ʿalayhā al-ḍaʿfu tilka al-laylata kathīran fa-bittu wa-anā mutafakkirun
sentences.l: And I was troubled, while she (was) weak; and the weakness increased upon her that night greatly; and I spent-the-night, and I (was) pondering.
sentences.i: I was distressed, for she was weak, and that night her weakness increased greatly; I passed the night in anxious thought.
sentences.n: تَشَوَّشَ, "be troubled or confused," is a post-Classical verb, common in later Arabic but not in the old dictionaries.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ خَرَجْتُ مِنْ بَيْتِي وَ دُرْتُ عَلَى الْبَسَاتِينِ وَاحِدًا وَاحِدًا فَامْ أَجِدْهُ فِيهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu kharajtu min baytī wa-durtu ʿalā al-basātīni wāḥidan wāḥidan fa-ām ajidhu fīhā
sentences.l: And when the morning became-morning, I went-out from my house and went-round upon the orchards, one by one; and I did not find it in them.
sentences.i: When morning came I left my house and went round the orchards one by one, but found none in them.
sentences.n: The edition prints فام, which is evidently a slip for فَلَمْ ("and not"); the lām has dropped out. I keep the printed letters and point them so that they read as فَلَمْ would.

sentences.t: فَصَادَفَنِي خُولِيٌّ كَبِيرٌ فَسَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ التُّفَّاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣādafanī khūliyyun kabīrun fa-saʾaltuhu ʿani al-tuffāḥi
sentences.l: And there met me an old gardener; and I asked him about the apples.
sentences.i: I met an aged gardener and asked him about apples.
sentences.n: خُولِيّ is the Egyptian word for a steward or head gardener; كَبِير here means aged or senior.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا وَلَدِي هَذَا شَيْ قَلَّ أَنْ يُوجَدَ وَهُوَ مَعْلُومٌ وَلَا يُوجَدُ إِلَّا فِي بُسْتَانِ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الَّذِي فِى الْبَصْرَةِ وَهُوَ عِنْدَ الْخُولِيِّ يَدَّخِرُهُ لِلْخَلِيفَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā waladī hādhā shayʾ qalla an yūjada wa-huwa maʿlūmun wa-lā yūjadu illā fī bustāni amīri al-muʾminīna alladhī fī al-Baṣrati wa-huwa ʿinda al-khūliyyi yaddakhiruhu li-al-khalīfati
sentences.l: And he said: O my son, this is a thing that it is-rare to be-found, and it is known; and it is not found except in the orchard of the commander of the Faithful which is in Basra; and it is with the gardener; he stores it for the caliph.
sentences.i: He said: My son, this is a rare thing, hard to find, and it is well known that it is found only in the garden of the Commander of the Faithful in Basra, where the gardener keeps it for the caliph.
sentences.n: The edition prints شي, which I read shayʾ (the final hamza is not written). قَلَّ أَنْ يُوجَدَ means "it is seldom found": قَلَّ with أَنْ takes on a negative sense.

sentences.t: فَجِئْتُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَدْ حَمَلَتْنِي مَحَبَّتِي لَهَا وَمَوَدَّتِى عَلَى أَنْ سَافَرْتُ وَهَيَّأْتُ لِي نَفْسِي وَسَافَرْتُ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا فِى الذَّهَابِ وَالْإِيَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-jiʾtu ilā al-bayti wa-qad ḥamalatnī maḥabbatī lahā wa-mawaddatī ʿalā an sāfartu wa-hayyaʾtu lī nafsī wa-sāfartu khamsata ʿashara yawman laylan wa-nahāran fī al-dhahābi wa-al-iyābi
sentences.l: And I came to the house, and my love for her and my affection had carried me to travel; and I made-ready for myself my self, and I travelled fifteen days, night and day, in the going and the returning.
sentences.i: I came home, and my love and affection for her drove me to set out on a journey. I made myself ready and travelled fifteen days, night and day, there and back.
sentences.n: The edition prints وهيأت; I read هَيَّأْتُ لِي نَفْسِي, "I made myself ready" (the lām is a reflexive dative). One could also read هَيَّأَتْ, "my soul prepared for me," but the surrounding first-person verbs favour "I." خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا is the ordinary compound number.

sentences.t: وَجِئْتُ لَهَا ثَلَٰثَ تُفَّاحَاتٍ اشْتَرَيْتُهُمْ مِنْ خُولِيِّ الْبَصْرَةِ بِثَلَٰثَةِ دَنَانِيرَ وَدَخَلْتُ وَنَاوَلْتُهُمْ لَهَا فَلَمْ تَفْرَحْ بِهِمْ وَتَرَكْتُهُمْ عَنْ جَانِبِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-jiʾtu lahā thalātha tuffāḥātin ishtaraytuhum min khūliyyi al-Baṣrati bi-thalāthati danānīra wa-dakhaltu wa-nāwaltuhum lahā fa-lam tafraḥ bihim wa-tarakathum ʿan jānibihā
sentences.l: And I came for her (with) three apples, I bought them from the gardener of Basra for three dinars; and I entered, and handed-them to her, and she did not rejoice at them, and left them by her side.
sentences.i: I brought her three apples, which I had bought from the gardener of Basra for three dinars. I went in and handed them to her, but she took no pleasure in them and left them beside her.
sentences.n: The apples are referred to with the masculine plural pronoun هُمْ (اشتريتهم، ناولتهم، بهم، تركتهم), where Classical usage would have the feminine singular for a non-human plural; this is a Middle Arabic feature. بِثَلَٰثَةِ دَنَانِيرَ: bi- marks the price, "for three dinars." بِهِمْ after تَفْرَحْ: the verb فَرِحَ takes bi- for the thing one rejoices in.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ قَدْ زَادَ بِهَا الضَّعْفُ وَالْحُمَّى وَلَمْ تَزَلْ فِي ضَعْفِهَا إِلَى أَنْ مَضَى لَهَا عَشَرَةُ أَيَّامٍ وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ عُوفِيَتْ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna qad zāda bihā al-ḍaʿfu wa-al-ḥummā wa-lam tazal fī ḍaʿfihā ilā an maḍā lahā ʿasharatu ayyāmin wa-baʿda dhālika ʿūfiyat
sentences.l: And weakness and fever had increased in her; and she did not cease in her weakness until ten days passed for her, and after that she was restored-to-health.
sentences.i: Her weakness and fever had grown worse, and she remained in her weakness until ten days had passed, and after that she recovered.
sentences.n: The verb زَادَ agrees with the nearer singular الضَّعْفُ. لَمْ تَزَلْ means "she did not cease," that is, "she continued." عُوفِيَتْ is the passive of عَافَى, "be granted well-being."

sentences.t: فَخَرَجْتُ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ وَذَهَبْتُ إِلَى دُكَّانِي وَجَلَسْتُ فِي بَيْعِي وَشِرَائِي
sentences.tr: fa-kharajtu mina al-bayti wa-dhahabtu ilā dukkānī wa-jalastu fī bayʿī wa-shirāʾī
sentences.l: So I went out from the house, and went to my shop, and sat in my selling and my buying.
sentences.i: So I left the house, went to my shop, and sat down to my buying and selling.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا أَنَا جَالِسٌ وَسَطَ النَّهَارِ وَإِذَا بِعَبْدٍ أَسْوَدَ فَائِتٌ عَلَيَّ وَفِي يَدِهِ تُفَّاحَةٌ مِنْ تِلْكَ التُّفَّاحَاتِ الثَّلٰثِ يَلْعَبُ بِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā anā jālisun wasaṭa al-nahāri wa-idhā bi-ʿabdin aswada fāʾitun ʿalayya wa-fī yadihi tuffāḥatun min tilka al-tuffāḥāti al-thalāthi yalʿabu bihā
sentences.l: So while I (was) sitting mid-of the day, and behold — with a black slave passing over me, and in his hand an apple from those apples, the three, he plays with it.
sentences.i: One day, as I sat at midday, a black slave came past me with one of those three apples in his hand, playing with it.
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِعَبْدٍ is the "and behold" pattern: the بِـ after إِذَا of surprise only marks what appears. فَائِتٌ (printed with ئ) is read here as "passing by", from فَاتَ; it is a little unusual, and the sense "coming toward me" would be the more expected آتٍ. The clause يَلْعَبُ بِهَا is a circumstantial clause: "playing with it". The narrator is the young man of the story of the murdered wife, telling it to the caliph.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ يَا عَبْدَ الْخَيْرِ مِنْ أَيْنَ أَخَذْتَ هَذِهِ التُّفَّاحَةَ حَتَّى آخُذَ مِثْلَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu yā ʿabda al-khayri min ayna akhadhta hādhihi al-tuffāḥata ḥattā ākhudha mithlahā
sentences.l: So I said to him: O slave of the good, from where did you take this apple, so that I may take its like?
sentences.i: I said to him, "Good fellow, where did you get this apple, that I may get one like it?"
sentences.n: يَا عَبْدَ الْخَيْرِ, literally "slave of goodness", is a friendly form of address. حَتَّى with the subjunctive آخُذَ gives purpose: "so that I may take".

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ وَقَالَ أَخَذْتُهَا مِنْ حَبِيبَتِي وَأَنَا كُنْتُ غَائِبًا وَجِئْتُ فَوَجَدْتُهَا ضَعِيفَةً وَعِنْدَهَا ثَلٰثُ تُفَّاحَاتٍ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika wa-qāla akhadhtuhā min ḥabībatī wa-anā kuntu ghāʾiban wa-jiʾtu fa-wajadtuhā ḍaʿīfatan wa-ʿindahā thalāthu tuffāḥātin
sentences.l: So he laughed and said: I took it from my sweetheart; and I had been absent, and I came and found her weak, and with-her three apples.
sentences.i: He laughed and said, "I got it from my sweetheart. I had been away, and when I came I found her ailing, with three apples beside her.
sentences.n: ثَلٰثُ is the edition's spelling of ثَلَاثُ, with the alif omitted; it is pointed with the dagger alif so it strips back to what is printed. The slave's speech continues into the next unit.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ لِي إِنَّ زَوْجِي الْقَرْنَانَ سَافَرَ مِنْ شَانِهِمُ الْبَصْرَةَ اشْتَرَاهُمْ بِثَلٰثَةِ دَنَانِيرَ فَأَخَذْتُ مِنْهُمْ هَذِهِ التُّفَّاحَةَ
sentences.tr: qālat lī inna zawjī al-qarnāna sāfara min shānihimu al-Baṣrata ishtarāhum bi-thalāthati danānīra fa-akhadhtu minhum hādhihi al-tuffāḥata
sentences.l: She said to me: Indeed my husband, the cuckold, travelled for-their-sake (to) Basra; he-bought them for three dinars. So I took from them this apple.
sentences.i: She told me, 'My husband, that cuckold, travelled to Basra on their account and bought them for three dinars.' So I took this apple from among them."
sentences.n: مِنْ شَانِهِمْ "on account of them" is the colloquial min shān (Classical مِنْ أَجْلِهِمْ or مِنْ شَأْنِهِمْ); the printed word has no hamza, so it is pointed as printed. سَافَرَ … اشْتَرَاهُمْ places two verbs side by side with no conjunction, which is ordinary in narrative speech. الْقَرْنَانُ (Lane: a man without jealousy over his wife, a cuckold) is an insult the slave puts in the woman's mouth, and the slave repeats it to the husband himself without knowing who he is talking to.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ كَلَامَ الْعَبْدِ اسْوَدَّتِ الدُّنْيَا فِي وَجْهِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu yā amīra al-muʾminīna kalāma al-ʿabdi iswaddati al-dunyā fī wajhī
sentences.l: So when I heard, O Commander of the Faithful, the speech of the slave, the world blackened in my face.
sentences.i: When I heard the slave's words, O Commander of the Faithful, the world turned black before my eyes.
sentences.n: The address يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ is dropped in mid-sentence, between فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ and its object; the young man is speaking to the caliph. اسْوَدَّتِ الدُّنْيَا فِي وَجْهِي is the idiom for despair or fury: the world went dark. The alif of اسْوَدَّتْ is a joining alif, so the final tā takes a kasra before الدُّنْيَا.

sentences.t: وَقُمْتُ قَفَلْتُ دُكَّانِي وَجِئْتُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَأَنَا عَادِمُ الْعَقْلِ مِنْ شِدَّةِ الْغَيْظِ
sentences.tr: wa-qumtu qafaltu dukkānī wa-jiʾtu ilā al-bayti wa-anā ʿādimu al-ʿaqli min shiddati al-ghayẓi
sentences.l: And I rose, I locked my shop, and came to the house, and I (was) one-lacking the mind from the intensity of the rage.
sentences.i: I got up, shut my shop, and went home, out of my wits with rage.
sentences.n: وَقُمْتُ قَفَلْتُ sets two perfects side by side with no و; the first works like "I got up and". قَفَلَ "to lock" is the ordinary later-Arabic verb.

sentences.t: وَنَظَرْتُ إِلَى التُّفَّاحِ فَلَمْ أَجِدِ الِاثْنَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-naẓartu ilā al-tuffāḥi fa-lam ajidi al-ithnayni
sentences.l: And I looked at the apples, and did not find the two.
sentences.i: I looked at the apples and could not find the other two.
sentences.n: الِاثْنَيْنِ "the two" means the two apples missing from the three. The kasra on the last letter of أَجِدِ is the linking vowel before the joining alif of الِاثْنَيْنِ.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا أَيْنَ الثَّالِثَةُ فَقَالَتْ لَا أَدْرِي وَلَا أَعْرِفُ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā ayna al-thālithatu fa-qālat lā adrī wa-lā aʿrifu
sentences.l: So I said to her: Where (is) the third? And she said: I do not know, and I am not aware.
sentences.i: I said to her, "Where is the third?" and she said, "I do not know, and I have no idea."

sentences.t: فَتَحَقَّقْتُ قَوْلَ الْعَبْدِ
sentences.tr: fa-taḥaqqaqtu qawla al-ʿabdi
sentences.l: So I made-certain the saying of the slave.
sentences.i: So I was convinced that the slave had spoken the truth.
sentences.n: تَحَقَّقَ with a direct object means "to ascertain, to hold as established"; the husband takes the wife's evasion as proof that she has given the third apple away.

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ وَأَخَذْتُ سِكِّينًا وَجِئْتُ مِنْ خَلْفِهَا وَمَا كَلَّمْتُهَا حَتَّى رَكِبْتُ عَلَى صَدْرِهَا وَنَحَرْتُهَا بِالسِّكِّينِ وَقَطَعْتُ رَأْسَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu wa-akhadhtu sikkīnan wa-jiʾtu min khalfihā wa-mā kallamtuhā ḥattā rakibtu ʿalā ṣadrihā wa-naḥartuhā bi-al-sikkīni wa-qaṭaʿtu raʾsahā
sentences.l: So I rose and took a knife, and came from behind her, and did not speak to her until I mounted upon her chest, and slit-her-throat with the knife, and cut off her head.
sentences.i: I rose, took a knife, and came at her from behind; without a word to her I climbed onto her chest, cut her throat with the knife, and severed her head.
sentences.n: نَحَرَ is to strike at the نَحْر, the top of the chest at the base of the throat (Lane), the way an animal is slaughtered. The edition prints رَأْسَهَا with a precomposed أ, so that letter is kept as printed. The sentence is delivered flatly, without softening, as it is in the Arabic.

sentences.t: وَحَطَّيْتُهَا فِى الْقُنَّةِ بِسُرْعَةٍ وَغَطَّيْتُهَا بِالْإِزَارِ وَخَيَّطْتُهَا
sentences.tr: wa-ḥaṭṭaytuhā fī al-qunnati bi-surʿatin wa-ghaṭṭaytuhā bi-al-izāri wa-khayyaṭtuhā
sentences.l: And I put her in the container quickly, and covered her with the wrap, and stitched her (up).
sentences.i: Quickly I put her into the basket, covered her with the wrap, and stitched it shut.
sentences.n: حَطَّ "to put, set down" is the colloquial verb (Classical وَضَعَ). الْقُنَّة is printed as such and is obscure: a قُنَّة is a small vessel or a peak, neither of which one sews shut. Since the next verb is "stitched", a misprint for الْقُفَّة "the basket" is likely, but this is a guess, and the edition's word is kept. Likewise خَيَّطْتُهَا, "I stitched her", most naturally means stitching the covering shut over the container.

sentences.t: وَ حَطَّيْتُ عَلَيْهَا شُقَّةً مِنَ الْبِسَاطِ وَأَنْزَلْتُهَا الصُّنْدُوقَ وَقَفَلْتُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥaṭṭaytu ʿalayhā shuqqatan mina al-bisāṭi wa-anzaltuhā al-ṣundūqa wa-qafaltuhu
sentences.l: And I put over her a piece of the carpet, and lowered her (into) the chest, and locked it.
sentences.i: Over her I laid a piece of carpet, lowered her into the chest, and locked it.
sentences.n: The edition's line breaks after a detached و (end of the previous line); the two belong together and are read وَحَطَّيْتُ. أَنْزَلْتُهَا الصُّنْدُوقَ takes the chest as a bare accusative of place, without فِي.

sentences.t: وَحَمَلْتُهَا عَلَى بَغْلَتِي وَرَمَيْتُهَا فِى الدِّجْلَةِ بِيَدِي
sentences.tr: wa-ḥamaltuhā ʿalā baghlatī wa-ramaytuhā fī al-Dijlati bi-yadī
sentences.l: And I loaded her on my mule, and threw her into the Tigris with my hand.
sentences.i: I loaded her onto my mule and threw her into the Tigris with my own hands.
sentences.n: الدِّجْلَة is the Tigris with the article, which Classical usage does not normally add to دِجْلَة. بِيَدِي is "with my own hand", stressing that he did it himself.

sentences.t: فَبِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَجِّلْ بِشَنْقِي فَإِنِّي خَائِفٌ مِنْ مُطَالَبَتِهَا لِي يَوْمَ الْقِيٰمَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-bi-Allāhi ʿalayka yā amīra al-muʾminīna ʿajjil bi-shanqī fa-innī khāʾifun min muṭālabatihā lī yawma al-qiyāmati
sentences.l: So by God upon you, O Commander of the Faithful, hasten with my hanging, for I am afraid of her claim against me on the Day of the Resurrection.
sentences.i: So by God, Commander of the Faithful, make haste to hang me, for I fear her suit against me on the Day of Resurrection.
sentences.n: فَبِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ is an oath-formula of adjuration: "by God, upon you", that is "I beg you by God". الْقِيٰمَة is the edition's short spelling of الْقِيَامَةِ, kept as printed. The fear is that the murdered wife will bring her claim against him at the Judgment.

sentences.t: فَإِنِّي لَمَّا رَمَيْتُهَا فِي بَحْرِ الدِّجْلَةِ وَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِهَا أَحَدٌ رَجَعْتُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَجَدْتُ وَلَدِى الْكَبِيرَ يَبْكِي
sentences.tr: fa-innī lammā ramaytuhā fī baḥri al-Dijlati wa-lam yaʿlam bihā aḥadun rajaʿtu ilā al-bayti wajadtu waladī al-kabīra yabkī
sentences.l: For I — when I had thrown her into the sea of the Tigris, and no one had known of her — returned to the house (and) found my eldest son weeping.
sentences.i: For when I had thrown her into the Tigris, and no one knew of it, I went back home and found my eldest son weeping.
sentences.n: The فَإِنِّي is resumptive: it picks up the plea for haste and explains it, and the sentence does not finish until رَجَعْتُ. The Arabic literally says "the sea of the Tigris", a big-river usage. وَجَدْتُ follows رَجَعْتُ with no و, and the printed وَلَدِى ends in ى, the edition's way of writing the possessive; it is read as the object, "my son".

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ عِلْمٌ بِمَا فَعَلْتُ فِي أُمِّهِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yakun lahu ʿilmun bi-mā faʿaltu fī ummihi
sentences.l: And there was not to him knowledge of what I had done in (the matter of) his mother.
sentences.i: He knew nothing of what I had done to his mother.
sentences.n: فَعَلْتُ فِي أُمِّهِ, with فِي "in", is "what I did to his mother".

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ مَا يُبْكِيكَ يَا وَلَدِى
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu mā yubkīka yā waladī
sentences.l: So I said to him: What makes-you-weep, O my son?
sentences.i: I said to him, "What is making you cry, my son?"

sentences.t: فَقٰلَ إِنِّي أَخَذْتُ تُفَّاحَةً مِنَ التُّفَّاحِ الَّذِي عِنْدَ أُمِّي وَنَزَلْتُ بِهَا إِلَى الزُّقَاقِ أَلْعَبُ مَعَ إِخْوَتِي وَإِذَا بِعَبْدٍ أَسْوَدَ طَوِيلٍ خَطَفَهَا مِنِّي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla innī akhadhtu tuffāḥatan mina al-tuffāḥi alladhī ʿinda ummī wa-nazaltu bihā ilā al-zuqāqi alʿabu maʿa ikhwatī wa-idhā bi-ʿabdin aswada ṭawīlin khaṭafahā minnī
sentences.l: So he said: I took an apple from the apples which (are) with my mother, and went down with it to the alley, I play with my brothers, and behold — a slave, black, tall, snatched it from me.
sentences.i: He said, "I took an apple from the apples my mother had, and went down with it to the lane to play with my brothers, and suddenly a tall black slave snatched it from me.
sentences.n: The printed فقل is a defective spelling of فَقَالَ, so it is pointed with the dagger alif to give فَقَٰلَ. نَزَلْتُ بِهَا is "I went down with it": the بِـ makes the verb carry the object along. أَلْعَبُ is a circumstantial clause "(while) I play", in the present tense.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِي هَذِةِ جَاءَتْكَ مِنْ أَيْنَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lī hādhihi jāʾatka min ayna
sentences.l: And he said to me: This one, from where came-it to you?
sentences.i: He said to me, 'Where did you get this?'
sentences.n: The edition prints هذة with a final ة, kept as printed; it is read هَذِهِ. The word order is colloquial: the demonstrative first, then the verb with its pronoun, then the question word at the end.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ هَذِهِ سَافَرَ لَهَا أَبِي وَجَاءَ بِهَا مِنَ الْبَصْرَةِ مِنْ أَجْلِ أُمِّي وَهِيَ ضَعِيفَةٌ وَاشْتَرَى ثَلٰثَ تُفَّاحَاتٍ بِثَلٰثَةِ دَنَانِيرَ ثُمَّ أَخَذَهَا وَلَمْ يَلْتَفِتْ إِلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu hādhihi sāfara lahā abī wa-jāʾa bihā mina al-Baṣrati min ajli ummī wa-hiya ḍaʿīfatun wa-ishtarā thalātha tuffāḥātin bi-thalāthati danānīra thumma akhadhahā wa-lam yaltafit ilayya
sentences.l: So I said to him: This one, my father travelled for it, and brought it from Basra, for the sake of my mother, and she (is) weak, and he bought three apples for three dinars. Then he took it, and did not turn to me.
sentences.i: I said to him, 'My father travelled for this apple and brought it from Basra for my mother, who is ill; he bought three apples for three dinars.' Then he took it and paid me no heed.
sentences.n: The boy retells the slave's words back to him. ثَلٰثَ … بِثَلٰثَةِ show the edition's short spelling of the numeral again. يَلْتَفِتْ is jussive after لَمْ, hence the kasra with sukūn.

sentences.t: فَعُدْتُ لَهُ الْقَوْلَ ثَانِيًا وَثَالِثًا وَلَمْ يَلْتَفِتْ إِلَيَّ وَضَرَبَنِي وَرَاحَ بِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿudtu lahu al-qawla thāniyan wa-thālithan wa-lam yaltafit ilayya wa-ḍarabanī wa-rāḥa bihā
sentences.l: So I repeated to him the saying a second time and a third, and he did not turn to me, and struck me, and went-off with it.
sentences.i: I said it to him again, a second time and a third, but he paid me no heed; he struck me and went off with it.
sentences.n: عَادَ لَهُ الْقَوْلَ is "he returned the saying to him", that is, repeated it. رَاحَ بِهَا is "he went off with it", with the same object-carrying بِـ as before.

sentences.t: فَخِفْتُ مِنْ أُمِّي تَضْرِبُنِي مِنْ شَانِ التُّفَّاحَةِ فَغِبْتُ أَنَا وَإِخْوَتِي مِنْ خَوْفِهَا إِلَى ظَاهِرِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَقَدْ أَمْسَى الْمَسَاءُ عَلَيْنَا وَأَنَا خَائِفٌ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-khiftu min ummī taḍribunī min shāni al-tuffāḥati fa-ghibtu anā wa-ikhwatī min khawfihā ilā ẓāhiri al-madīnati wa-qad amsā al-masāʾu ʿalaynā wa-anā khāʾifun minhā
sentences.l: So I feared (that) my mother (would) strike me because-of the apple, and I stayed-away, I and my brothers, from fear of her, to the outside of the city; and the evening had come upon us, and I (was) afraid of her.
sentences.i: I was afraid my mother would beat me over the apple, so out of fear of her my brothers and I stayed away, out beyond the city walls, and evening fell on us while I was still afraid of her.
sentences.n: خِفْتُ مِنْ أُمِّي تَضْرِبُنِي has no أَنْ before the verb; the indicative تَضْرِبُنِي "(that) she would strike me" is the loose construction of ordinary speech. مِنْ شَانِ again is colloquial "because of".

sentences.t: فَبِاللَّهِ يَا أَبِي لَا تَقُلْ لَهَا شَيْئًا تَزْدَادُ ضَعْفًا عَلَى ضَعْفِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-bi-Allāhi yā abī lā taqul lahā shayʾan tazdādu ḍaʿfan ʿalā ḍaʿfihā
sentences.l: So by God, O my father, do not say to her anything — she increases (in) weakness upon her weakness.
sentences.i: So by God, Father, say nothing to her, or she will grow weaker still.
sentences.n: تَزْدَادُ is pointed as printed, in the indicative. After a prohibition Classical Arabic would use a jussive (تَزْدَدْ) for "lest she"; here the clause simply follows, meaning "(else) she gets weaker".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ كَلَامَ الْوَلَدِ عَلِمْتُ أَنَّ الْعَبْدَ هُوَ الَّذِي افْتَرَى الْكَلَامَ الْكَذِبَ عَلَى بِنْتِ عَمِّي وَتَحَقَّقْتُ أَنَّهَا قُتِلَتْ ظُلْمًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu kalāma al-waladi ʿalimtu anna al-ʿabda huwa alladhī iftarā al-kalāma al-kadhiba ʿalā binti ʿammī wa-taḥaqqaqtu annahā qutilat ẓulman
sentences.l: So when I heard the speech of the boy, I knew that the slave, he (is) the one who forged the speech, the lie, against the daughter of my paternal-uncle, and I made-certain that she had been killed wrongfully.
sentences.i: When I heard the boy's words, I knew that it was the slave who had forged those lying words against my cousin, and I was certain that she had been killed unjustly.
sentences.n: بِنْتُ عَمِّي, "daughter of my father's brother", is the wife and a cousin; the old man who is present is her father, hence "my uncle" in the next sentence. الْكَلَامَ الْكَذِبَ puts the noun كَذِب "lie" after the article-carrying noun as if it were an adjective, "the lie-speech".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنِّي بَكَيْتُ بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا وَإِذَا بِهَذَا الشَّيْخِ وَهُوَ عَمِّي وَالِدُهَا قَدْ أَقْبَلَ فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ بِمَا كَانَ فَجَلَسَ بِجَانِبِي وَبَكَى
sentences.tr: thumma innī bakaytu bukāʾan shadīdan wa-idhā bi-hādhā al-shaykhi wa-huwa ʿammī wālidu-hā qad aqbala fa-akhbartuhu bi-mā kāna fa-jalasa bi-jānibī wa-bakā
sentences.l: Then I wept a violent weeping, and behold — this old man, and he (is) my paternal-uncle, her father, had come; and I informed him of what had been, and he sat at my side, and wept.
sentences.i: Then I wept bitterly, and behold, this old man, my uncle, her father, had come; I told him what had happened, and he sat beside me and wept.
sentences.n: بِهَذَا الشَّيْخِ: again the بِـ after إِذَا of surprise, only marking the newcomer. هَذَا الشَّيْخُ is the old man standing in the caliph's presence, the wife's father, and the demonstrative points at him. أَخْبَرْتُهُ بِمَا كَانَ is "I told him what had happened": the verb takes بِـ for the thing reported.

sentences.t: وَ لَمْ نَزَلْ نَبْكِي إِلَى نِصْفِ اللَّيْلِ وَأَقَمْنَا الْعَزَا خَمْسَةَ أَيَّامٍ لِهَذَا الْيَوْمِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam nazal nabkī ilā niṣfi al-layli wa-aqamnā al-ʿazā khamsata ayyāmin li-hādhā al-yawmi
sentences.l: And we did not cease weeping until the middle of the night, and we held the mourning five days, up-to this day.
sentences.i: We did not stop weeping until midnight, and we have kept the mourning for five days until today.
sentences.n: The printed و at the end of the previous line is detached from لَمْ; read وَلَمْ. الْعَزَا is the edition's spelling of الْعَزَاءِ, "mourning". لِهَذَا الْيَوْمِ uses لِـ to mean "up to, as of": five days up to this very day.

sentences.t: وَنَحْنُ نَتَأَسَّفُ عَلَى قَتْلِهَا ظُلْمًا
sentences.tr: wa-naḥnu nataʾassafu ʿalā qatlihā ẓulman
sentences.l: And we (are) grieving over her killing, wrongfully.
sentences.i: And we grieve over her unjust killing.
sentences.n: The edition prints نَتَأَسَّفُ with a precomposed أ, kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَكُلُّ ذَلِكَ كَانَ مِنْ تَحْتِ رَأْسِ الْبُعْدِ وَهَذَا سَبَبُ قَتْلِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-kullu dhālika kāna min taḥti raʾsi al-buʿdi wa-hādhā sababu qatlihā
sentences.l: And all that was from under the head of the "distance" (sic: read the slave), and this (is) the cause of her killing.
sentences.i: All of it came at the instigation of the slave, and this is the reason she was killed.
sentences.n: The printed الْبُعْد "the distance" makes no sense here and is almost certainly a transposition of the letters of الْعَبْد "the slave"; the printed letters are kept, so the word is pointed as printed, and the translation follows the sense. مِنْ تَحْتِ رَأْسِ فُلَانٍ, "from under someone's head", is the idiom for "at someone's doing".

sentences.t: فَبِحُرْمَةِ أَجْدَادِكَ عَجِّلْ بِقَتْلِي فَلَا حَيٰوةَ لِي بَعْدَهَا وَخُذْحَقَّهَا مِنِّي
sentences.tr: fa-bi-ḥurmati ajdādika ʿajjil bi-qatlī fa-lā ḥayāta lī baʿdahā wa-khudh ḥaqqahā minnī
sentences.l: So by the sanctity of your forefathers, hasten with my killing, for there is no life for me after her, and take her right from me.
sentences.i: So by the honour of your forefathers, hasten my execution, for I have no life after her; take her due from me.
sentences.n: The edition prints وخذحقها as one run-together word (وَخُذْ + حَقَّهَا), and the unit keeps it so; it is read as two words. حَيٰوة is the older spelling of حَيَاة with a wāw, read ḥayāh, and pointed with the dagger alif. بِحُرْمَةِ is an oath: "by the sanctity of".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْخَلِيفَةُ كَلَامَ الشَّابِّ تَعَجَّبَ وَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ لَا أَشْنُقُ إِلَّا الْعَبْدَ الْمَلْعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-khalīfatu kalāma al-shābbi taʿajjaba wa-qāla wa-Allāhi lā ashnuqu illā al-ʿabda al-malʿūna
sentences.l: So when the caliph heard the speech of the youth he marvelled, and said: By God, I shall not hang except the accursed slave.
sentences.i: When the caliph heard the young man's words he was amazed, and said, "By God, I will hang no one but the accursed slave,

sentences.t: وَلَا عْمَلُ عَمَلًا يُشْفَى الْعَلِيلُ وَيَرْضَى الْمَلِكُ الْجَلِيلُ
sentences.tr: wa-lāʿmalu ʿamalan yushfā al-ʿalīlu wa-yarḍā al-maliku al-jalīlu
sentences.l: And I shall surely do a deed (by which) the sick is healed and the Majestic King is pleased.
sentences.i: and I will do a deed by which the sick are healed and the Majestic King is well pleased."
sentences.n: The printed ولا عمل is two words. It is read as وَلَأَعْمَلُ, "and I shall surely do", with the oath-lām la- and the verb aʿmalu, whose two a-sounds merge in speech (la + aʿmalu becomes lāʿmalu); the usual emphatic nūn (لَأَعْمَلَنَّ) is not written. Another reading, with يُشْفِي … يُرْضِي ("heals the sick, pleases the King"), is also possible. الْمَلِكُ الْجَلِيلُ, the Majestic King, is God; الْعَلِيلُ / الْجَلِيلُ is a rhyme.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, breaking off the tale she was free to tell.
sentences.n: The night-closing formula. شَهْرَزَادَ is diptote, hence the fatḥa. الصَّبَاحُ / الْمُبَاحِ rhymes; الْكَلَامُ الْمُبَاحُ, "the permitted speech", is the story that she is allowed to tell.
